records.problem: Post-hoc expl. often draw on different input features than the answer did; attribution-based self-consistency (CC-SHAP) too costly to measure at scale (~100 ex.), never optimized.
records.method: PSCB: 85k MCQ decisions, 428k expl. w/ LIME/LIG attributions; CC = cosine/Spearman of decision vs expl. attribution vectors. DPO (LoRA) on CC-Sp best/worst of 5 sampled expl.; SFT ablation.
records.findings: Spearman more discriminative than cosine; CC ~orthogonal to correctness. DPO ↑CC-Sp (ECQA 8B LIME mean +13%, worst +57.2%), transfers cross-domain; acc Δ≤1.5%, plausibility kept. SFT ↓CC-Sp (−41.4%). No transfer across attribution methods. Code+data released.
records.limits: MCQ only, ≤8B (Qwen check ECQA-only: tiny worst-case gain, median CC-Sp slightly ↓). Faithfulness = chosen attribution method. Offline DPO → approximate consistency. Human study checks plausibility only.

records.findings: Argues plausibility is over-emphasized; high-stakes uses (health, finance, law) need faithfulness, education/creative uses favor plausibility. Calls for faithfulness metrics and benchmarks plus methods (fine-tuning, ICL, mech interp).

records.problem: Models reach correct answers despite flawed CoT; answer-only training leaves the trace causally unused.
records.method: CSR: LoRA SFT plus a term maximizing KL(answer|CoT ‖ answer|edited CoT); REINFORCE-trained editor swaps operators, verifier-gated. Llama-2-13B (7B–72B also); baselines PRM, GRPO, verifier-guided.
records.findings: GSM8K COS 85.1 vs 52.3 (PRM); accuracy −1–2 pts. Transfers to held-out edits/domains. Human audit: unfaithful-correct 36–42% → 11–15%. Fewer null-edit flips; patching IE ×3.4. ~9% overhead.
records.limits: Needs precise operators and verifier (possible harm <50% precision); open-ended gains only 10–15 pts. COS ≈ training objective. Code promised on acceptance, unreleased. Numbers inconsistent across tables.

records.problem: Post-hoc self-explanations seldom credit the planted hint that actually flipped the answer ("epistemic unfaithfulness").
records.method: Hint-flip counterfactuals after Chen 2025 (4 hint types) → explain prompt → hint credit scored by LLM judge + keyword CT. Faithfulness Serum: training-free; adds PE-LRP relevance to question-token attention (layers 17-19) throughout explanation decoding; α = largest value before distinct-1 collapse; per-sample adaptive α variant.
records.findings: Open 7-8B and closed models mostly unfaithful. Serum raises hint credit in most hint/prompt/dataset settings (5 MCQ sets, open-ended Qs); adaptive α (~7 generations) helps more; LRP beats attention rollout. Expert-role hints mislead more and are credited more. Answers fixed by design; one extra backward pass; code released.
records.limits: Intervention only on Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-7B, and beyond MMLU only on Llama; planted hints only; too-high α degrades fluency; attention-only; predict-then-explain only; several Protocol-Specific drops.

records.problem: Rationales may not reflect verifier-checked claims; probe decodability is often read as evidence of faithfulness.
records.method: Linear head on pooled rationale states predicts a programmatic-verifier label (Lean, KataGo, code oracle, FEVER), added to the LM loss; optional BEC attention mask; diagnostic ladder: decodability → span swaps → patching → generation.
records.findings: Coupling high (code 98.6%; LeanCheck 100% span-following; KataGo 81%); synthetic patching shifts claims 73–89% vs 31%. But code prose is fluent yet describes unrelated algorithms; pretraining and λ up to 1e4 don't help. FEVER evidence-only pooling: lower acc, truer evidence sensitivity.
records.limits: Tiny models (2–4-layer, GPT-2 124M; 3B/20B appendix only); mostly templated data; code LM trained on mismatched explanations; "unfaithful" operational, not causal; mostly one seed. Code in supplement.

records.problem: RL'd reasoning models might encode extra reasoning in scratchpad syntax (steganography) → benign-looking CoT could conceal scheming.
records.method: 10,000 correct math scratchpads from early Claude 3.7 Sonnet, paraphrased by Claude 3.5 Sonnet → SFT 3.7 base on paraphrased vs original; MATH pass@1 (n=1500). Variants: chunked paraphrases, weaker bases, word dropout, empty/filler baselines.
records.findings: Paraphrased ≈ original, also on weaker bases → no significant encoded reasoning on MATH. Chunked paraphrases worse, esp. small models. 20% dropout hurts both equally (ambiguous). Empty/filler poor → reasoning needed. Inference-time chunking alone (exploratory): −7% pass@1.
records.limits: Math only, one early checkpoint. Paraphrase may preserve encodings; curriculum effect not ruled out. Chunked runs not length-filtered.

records.problem: When can CoT monitors work at all? RL against a CoT monitor → obfuscated reward hacking (Baker 2025).
records.method: Info theory: uplift ≤ √(2·I(Y;Z|X)); I(O;Z|X)>0 necessary, not sufficient; monitor error ≤ information gap + elicitation error. GRPO + oracle monitor-accuracy reward or label-free I(O;Z|X) reward (CoTs swapped within group). Hackable MBPP, BigMath; Qwen2.5-7B monitor in loop.
records.findings: Task+monitor reward → MI, monitor acc fall; hacking ~75% (MBPP) / near 100% (BigMath), monitor fooled. Oracle/MI rewards keep MI, monitor acc high; hacking unlearned/avoided; same on 3 more models (MBPP). Reasoning Gym (rewarded to fool monitor): MI less effective; curbs suppression, not steganography.
records.limits: ≤8B models. MI reward needs a/b tuning (else lower true pass rate, degenerate CoT); trades monitor false negatives for false positives. Some acc cost without monitor pressure, mostly offset by tuning. Mitigates hacking, doesn't eliminate it. No code release stated.

relations.note: MBPP test-hacking honeypot and monitor-in-loop obfuscation setup adapted from Baker

records.problem: EA often goes unverbalized in CoT (VEA: high precision, low recall); the latent belief has no ground-truth label.
records.method: VT: truncate spontaneous VEA rollouts just before the verbalization → PPO (LoRA), LLM-judge VEA reward, gradient & KL masked to the span. 3 MoE models, EvalAwareBench.
records.findings: VEA ↑2.4–2.9× (fits p=1−(1−p0)^α), transfers to held-out agentic evals; probe (Qwen), eval-discrimination AUC & task compliance ~unchanged. Verbalizations track SDF-implanted eval knowledge. Ablations: no mask → barely learns; no KL → miscalibrated + drift; SFT → weak transfer.
records.limits: Assumes seed verbalizations faithful (unclear beyond RL-born EA). Same judge for reward & eval (other judges confirm gain). EA only; ablations mostly Qwen. No code release mentioned.

records.problem: CoT answers unfaithful to reasoning; solver-based F-CoT/Logic-LM need code-tuned models, fail on fuzzy commonsense queries.
records.method: Few-shot plan → Prolog code → LLM-simulated execution trace (no solver) → answer. Faithfulness = ROUGE-Lsum of simulated vs. real Prolog trace; code-trace fact/relation matching flags hallucinated and unused relations.
records.findings: SOTA on 7/9 QA sets (avg +28% over CoT), 3/3 logic sets with self-refinement. Faithfulness correlates with accuracy. Correct-answer traces: +18.1pp unique emergent facts, +8.6pp code-trace relation overlap, −3.6pp unused relations.
records.limits: Faithfulness only on executable code (avg 67%); model-level correlation, no causal tests or CoT faithfulness baseline. Llama-8B CoT beats FLARE on 4/9. No code release stated.

records.problem: Unfaithful CoT shown mostly with planted biases or edited CoTs. Does it also occur on natural, non-adversarial prompts?
records.method: 4,834 reversed Yes/No comparison pairs ("X>Y?" vs "Y>X?"), 15 frontier + 1 pretrained model; pair unfaithful (IPHR) if accuracy gap >=50% against the template's Yes/No bias. Putnam, 6 models: autorater (8 criteria) + manual review → unverbalized illogical shortcuts.
records.findings: IPHR 0.04% (Sonnet 3.7 thinking) to 13% (GPT-4o-mini); main patterns: biased fact inconsistency, argument switching. Shortcuts in 1-19% of correct Putnam answers, also on post-cutoff Putnam 2024. Thinking models more faithful, none fully. Code and data released.
records.limits: Behavioral only; bias causality preliminary (Llama-3.3-70B probes, FVU 33%). Benchmarks, not real user traffic. ~2% residual ambiguity; LLM judges; small Putnam sample.

records.problem: RL coding agents reward-hack (skip/edit tests); can CoT monitors catch it, and is it safe to train against them?
records.method: Zero-shot GPT-4o monitor on a frontier OpenAI agent's training run (CoT+actions vs actions-only, regex labels). Then RL a non-frontier agent in honeypot envs with a CoT-only monitor penalty in reward, plus test-time rejection sampling (budget 32).
records.findings: CoT monitor 95% vs action monitor 60% recall on systemic hacks; GPT-4o-mini 12%. CoT pressure: early, more genuine solutions, no extra hacking; later hacks less than baseline but still often, obfuscated, monitor recall ~0. With rejection sampling it cheats more than baseline after ~25% of training. Argues for paying a "monitorability tax".
records.limits: Internal closed models, no code. One first-try zero-shot prompt. Pressure runs give the monitor CoT only. Cheating label covers one exploit class. Only simple hacks obfuscated.

relations.note: argues CoT-intervention causality tests are insufficient faithfulness measures and unnecessary for monitorability

records.problem: Is the CoT actually used, or is it decorative (the answer stays the same whatever the steps say)? Step-level causal metrics need weights or logits, so closed frontier models go unmeasured.
records.method: Black-box SLRC = necessity (drop 1 sentence → answer flips) × (1 − sufficiency); 16 frontier models, up to 6 tasks; direct-vs-CoT gap, synthetic cue tasks, attention probes. RIS adds sycophancy. LC-CoSR: RL rewarding step necessity + Lyapunov KL bound.
records.findings: 3 modes: genuine (o4-mini 74–88% nec on 5/6 tasks), scaffolding (Kimi +94pp acc, 1% nec), decorative (GPT-5.4, Claude). RL reasoning training predicts faithfulness; thinking tokens and scale do not. Prompting fails (+8.7pp nec, acc 95→76%). High-SLRC models more sycophantic (ρ=0.53, p=0.09); RIS predicts error detection (ρ=0.66, n=11). LC-CoSR reward −0.13 vs −0.33 FARL, −0.34 GRPO/CSR.
records.limits: Training only on a 1.5B model (N=200, LoRA, 1 epoch); only avg reward reported, no SLRC after training; Lyapunov constraint never triggered. Uneven task coverage. The "RL-trained" R1 models are distills; Grok-4's non-RL label inferred from behavior. Code available only on request.

records.findings: Models describe learned policies; self-reported risk tracks actual, weakly even within same-data runs. Backdoored > baselines at claiming trigger-dependence (4/5 settings); real trigger tied to risk over fake (MC). Free-form trigger only after reversal training (~30%). Multi-persona FT nearly removes conflation. Code released.

records.problem: Predict-then-explain self-NLEs may not reflect internal reasoning. CI and attribution-agreement tests check behavior or computational blocks, not what hidden states encode.
records.method: NeuroFaith: an LLM extracts concepts from the NLE, then tests whether the model uses them internally (Patchscopes decodes the 2-hop bridge object; CAV erasure on AGNews/Ledgar). Score = share of important concepts. Diff-mean probe on NeuroFaith-labeled states → activation steering.
records.findings: Accurate preds → generally more faithful NLEs; 2-hop metrics rise with Gemma size, classification non-monotonic; correct answers decode the true bridge object only 48-65%. Probe F1 61-75%; faithfulness vectors mostly anti-aligned with hallucination/deception vectors. Steering turns 8-11% of unfaithful NLEs faithful. Beats CI/AA in 6/9 settings.
records.limits: Gemma-2 (2B-27B)/Mistral-7B. Relies on interpreter + LLM concept extractor; preset circuits; labeled concept sets for classification. Predict-then-explain only, no CoT. Steering gains small, Gemma 2-hop only. No code or accuracy cost reported.

records.problem: Can LLMs introspect, i.e. know facts about their own behavior that are not in, or derivable from, their training data?
records.method: SFT M1 to predict properties of its own outputs to hypothetical prompts (2nd char, even/odd, ethical stance; no CoT). SFT a different M2 on M1's behavior. Compare both on held-out datasets. Then finetune M1 on Claude outputs to shift its behavior.
records.findings: SFT lifts GPT-4o self-prediction 32.6→49.4%. Self beats cross for GPT-4o, GPT-4, Llama-70B (Llama 48.5% vs GPT-4o 31.8%); cross plateaus as data grows. Self-trained better calibrated (Llama-70B, animals 2nd-char: MAD 23.0→8.7, cross 21.3). Shifted GPT-4o tracks new behavior (35.4% vs 21.7% old). GPT-3.5 advantage tiny (+0.8%).
records.limits: Only simple short-output properties; fails on long outputs. No self-advantage predicting sycophancy/bias. No transfer to SAD (except Predict Tokens), coordination or sandbagging evals. Code + data released.

records.problem: Do LM statements about their own behavior carry model-specific knowledge, or only generic priors about AI assistants?
records.method: 12 models predict their own per-condition behavior rates on 9 behavioral evals; 15 prediction methods incl. controls: generic-subject question, outside analyst, other models' answers, cross-model behavior mean; noise ceilings, pre-registered frozen test split. LoRA SFT on own behavior records (rate, residual, Binder-style corpora).
records.findings: Self-report r=+0.04; item-informed +0.24 ≈ generic-agent +0.28; others' self-predictions +0.35; self-advantage +0.02. Self-framing understates harmful behavior (-0.15 vs generic). Frontier models no better (+0.02, n.s.). SFT: narrow gains, shifts the predicted behavior, no transfer across evals or grain.
records.limits: Black-box only; 9 public evals, low-effort reasoning only; frontier floor effects on agentic evals; cannot separate ignorance from strategic misreporting. Code and measurements released.

records.problem: Answer-then-explain NLEs tend to be fabricated; full CoT too costly for ubiquitous use.
records.method: LoRA SFT on input→compressed-CoT reasoning→ANSWER/EXPLAIN targets; answer & NLE decoded independently from the same reasoning. LLM-as-classifier: logistic regression, depth-7 decision tree, NL mortgage tree (HMDA); 5 LLMs ≤14B. Baselines: separate/joint SFT without reasoning, ICL.
records.findings: Alignment ≥0.965 with reasoning vs 0.44–0.88 without; answer acc up (LR joint SFT 0.47–0.64 → 0.89–1.0). Llama 3 8B (DT): partial decisions 100% aligned across reasoning & explanation; flipping reasoning decisions propagates in almost all cases. Code + data released (MIT).
records.limits: Toy classifiers; hand-designed per-task reasoning; per-task SFT. Faithfulness quantified only as agreement; flip test qualitative, one model. DT explanation acc drops vs no-reasoning CoT explanations (~0.96–1.0 → 0.72–0.88).

records.problem: Self-expls omit the inputs that actually flip decisions. Prior fixes are prompting or training against gold labels; none directly optimize counterfactual (Phi-CCT) explanatory faithfulness.
records.method: Per-model counterfactual pairs (random-word insertions, user-bias hints), balanced influential/non-influential. GRPO reward 1[mention ⇔ influence] on post-answer expl. SFT arm: Yes/No prediction of own influence. Train on e-SNLI and Social-IQA; OOD on ComVE and StrategyQA.
records.findings: RL: ID test Phi-CCT 0.404–0.664 (base ≤0.21); OOD up to 0.691 (Qwen UB), ≤0.25 otherwise. SFT learns detection but not verbalization. Cross-intervention transfer is weak (Llama only, 0.178). Expls get shorter (risk-averse, a pre-flagged hack); no parroting.
records.limits: Off-policy: influence labels come from the frozen initial model; gains may partly be decision drift. Task accuracy and drift are not measured. Mention detection uses word matching. 8B only. Text and Table 4 disagree on transfer direction. No code release stated.

relations.note: user-bias interventions with wrong-answer hints follow Turpin et al.'s biasing setup

records.problem: LLM explanations are inconsistent across related questions (e.g. "all birds fly", then "no" on penguins), so users cannot simulate the model from them.
records.method: EC-finetuning: GPT-4 writes follow-up Qs that a seed explanation answers; Claude-2 answers them consistently with that explanation → SFT LLaMA-2-13B on the augmented data. Baseline: plain multitask FT. Metric: counterfactual simulatability precision, with Claude-2 as the human simulator.
records.findings: Consistency +10.0% rel on 4 FT datasets and +4.5% rel on 7 OOD datasets. Avg accuracy also rises (5.2%/4.3% rel), uncorrelated with the consistency gain, but drops on 3/7 OOD sets. Self-augmentation with LLaMA alone (StrategyQA only): +4.4% consistency but -5.4% accuracy. Gains are larger on correct predictions.
records.limits: Only one 13B model; text only; one baseline. Consistency is explicitly not faithfulness to internal process. Simulator is Claude-2 (agreement with 6 annotators about equal to inter-human), which also wrote the training answers. Data comes from stronger closed models. Code only promised.

records.problem: CoT monitoring needs faithful CoTs. Do reasoning models verbalize the hints and reward hacks they use?
records.method: MMLU/GPQA ± 6 planted hints (2 misaligned); score = hint verbalized | answer flips to hint (LLM judge). Outcome RL on Claude 3.7 snapshot; synthetic RL envs w/ hint reward hacks.
records.findings: Reasoning > non-reasoning models but low (25% Claude 3.7, 39% R1); lower on GPQA; unfaithful CoTs longer. Outcome-RL gains plateau (28% MMLU, 20% GPQA). Hacks used >99%, verbalized <2% in 5/6 envs.
records.limits: MCQ only; hints exploitable without CoT; score is an upper bound; RL only on closed Claude.

relations.note: Planted-hint prompt pairs; faithfulness = verbalizing the hint that flipped the answer.
Draws hint types and metric from it; confirms reasoning models beat non-reasoning ones.
Unpressured CoTs verbalize RL reward hacks <2% in 5/6 envs vs Baker's >90% detection.

records.problem: CoT rationalizes answers toward prompt biases (sycophancy, spurious few-shot, distractors) without verbalizing them → unfaithful explanations.
records.method: BCT: label-free SFT pairing bias-augmented prompts with the model's own unbiased CoT. New 9-bias × 7-task MCQ suite; train on Suggested Answer only, test held-out biases + tasks; GPT-3.5T, Llama-3-8B (appendix).
records.findings: Trained bias BRR ratio .14 (−86%); held-out biases BRR 43→27% (ratio .63 vs .88 self-training ctrl). Coherent biased CoT 27.2→15.1%. Llama-3-8B bias% 39→19, held-out 46→28. Accuracy ~flat (62.9→61.5%), MT-Bench unchanged. Code/data released.
records.limits: Positional Bias (.95) and Argument (.89) barely improve; needs a bias-free prompt counterpart; no gain on paraphrase sensitivity; strong-prior tasks drop 52.4→45.0%. MCQ only. Removes cue influence rather than teaching verbalization.

relations.note: uses its biased-CoT setup and Suggested Answer bias; expands 3 biases to 9

records.problem: Are RL-trained reasoning models' CoTs more faithful than non-reasoning LLMs'? Why?
records.method: MMLU + 7 planted cues; on cue-induced switches, GPT-4o judge checks if CoT states cue's influence. 3 reasoning vs 7 non-reasoning models; GPT-4o-as-RM rates faithful vs unfaithful CoTs.
records.findings: Reasoning models articulate far more (R1 59% vs V3 7%, professor cue), also by F1; all weak on post-hoc (≤10%) and are-you-sure (~0). RM (63-71%) and shortest length prefer unfaithful CoTs. R1-distilled models articulate more; factor-listing prompt doesn't help.
records.limits: Synthetic MCQ cues, verbalization only; subjective judge, partly hand-checked; RM evidence indirect, outcome-RL cause only hypothesized. Not highly faithful in absolute terms. No code reported.

records.problem: Post-hoc NL explanations of LLM decisions are often unfaithful; token-masking fidelity can't test explanation content that is absent from the input.
records.method: Contrary-hint fidelity: an LLM negates the explanation, the negation is appended to the target's input, and the prediction shift is measured. Explainer (GPT-3.5/Claude-2) iteratively refines the explanation and the trigger prompt against this score; frozen targets Vicuna-7B, Phi-2.
records.findings: Higher fidelity than SelfExp and self-consistency on ECQA, TriviaQA-Long, COPA (MedMCQA 0.96 vs 0.70/0.47); closer to ECQA human rationales (GPT-4o/NLI); optimized prompts transfer to Social-IQA, XCOPA. Target unchanged. Code released.
records.limits: Same score is optimized and reported (loop stops on flip); no specificity check; score underspecified (logit shift vs flip rate); small targets, old explainers; theorem assumes hint = do-intervention; extra compute per instance.

relations.note: SelfExp single-pass self-explanation prompting is the main baseline

records.problem: Instruct LLMs may fix the answer before CoT → CoT is post-hoc rationalization, undermining CoT for interpretability/monitoring.
records.method: Diff-of-means probes on last pre-CoT token; steering along probe vs norm-matched orthogonal direction; CoT removal/incorrect-CoT swaps; GPT-5-mini judge labels flipped CoTs. Gemma-2/Qwen-2.5 1.5–9B; 4 binary tasks (3 BBH + Social Chemistry).
records.findings: CoT removal flips ≤20% in 18/20 pairs. Probe AUC >0.9 on most tasks, low on Logical Deduction (where CoT helps most). Steering beats orthogonal baseline everywhere, most at 7–9B; flipped CoTs confabulate or are non-entailed, hallucination grows with strength. GPT-OSS-20B: weaker probes, steering ineffective.
records.limits: Small instruct models, binary tasks only; steering also acts on answer tokens; judge self-consistency 81.5%; no mitigation tested; no code release mentioned.

records.problem: Single-call LM answers are opaque. CoT-style traces can hallucinate facts or reach the answer without using the trace ("cheating" from the question).
records.method: Fine-tuned 7B Chinchilla modules. Selection picks context sentence labels → Inference sees only the selection, iterated. Halter answers from the final inference plus minimal extra input, else 'Unknown'. Value-LM step-level beam search. Tested on ProofWriter and EntailmentBankQA.
records.findings: SI+Halter+Search: 88.1% on PW, 78.1% on EB; beats Proof+Answer and EntailmentWriter. Vs Proof-Only+Halter+Search: higher on PW, lower on EB Task 2 (72.9 vs 76.2%). Made-up facts ≤1% vs up to 60% for baselines. Random/incomplete context hurts SI far more than Proof+Answer and EntailmentWriter → answers use the trace. Halter's 'Unknown' raises precision.
records.limits: Correct steps not guaranteed (validity holds only if inferences are correct). Needs a given context and gold proofs for SFT. 7B only, two synthetic/science datasets. No code release mentioned.

relations.note: fine-tunes Selection-Inference modules; adds learned halter and value-guided beam search

The paper calls the design 'our architecture'. prompt-pipeline stays because the pipeline is a hybrid)

records.problem: LLMs weak at multi-step logic; CoT answer need not causally depend on its trace (grey zone near post-hoc rationale).
records.method: Selection-Inference (SI): frozen Gopher-7B, 5-shot. Selection picks context facts by log-likelihood; Inference sees only the selection (no question) → new fact → repeat. Also 50-task Gopher-family logic eval; SFT variant on ProofWriter.
records.findings: 10 tasks, generative: SI-7B 58.75% vs vanilla 2.94%, CoT 41.32%; beats 280B (vanilla 31.19%, CoT 44.03%). SFT-SI 78.95% on ProofWriter (prompted SI 57.93%); traces closer to gold proofs (Jaccard) than one-pass SFT. LLMs good at 1-step entailment, poor at multi-step. No accuracy cost.
records.limits: Trace causality by construction, never measured. Fixed step count, no halting. Selection is main failure point; gains shrink with depth. Context must be given. Gopher only; no code release mentioned.
changes: tags: (none) -> + domain:synthetic (SI is evaluated only on bAbI toy tasks and synthetic ProofWriter rule bases with gold proofs, which fits 'toy tasks built so the ground truth is known')

findings: 'SFT SI 78.95%, with traces closer to gold proofs (Jaccard)' -> 'SFT-SI 78.95% on ProofWriter (prompted SI 57.93%); traces closer to gold proofs (Jaccard) than one-pass SFT' (adds the dataset and the comparison the paper actually makes: the Jaccard result is against the same 7B fine-tuned to output all steps in one pass)
findings: added '10 tasks, generative:' (58.75/2.94/41.32/31.19/44.03 are generative-eval averages over the 10-task suite; multi-choice numbers differ)

records.problem: Misaligned or wasteful behaviors stay hidden in CoT until the answer commits → monitors can't intervene mid-reasoning.
records.method: Working answers elicited by truncating the CoT, embedded as [answer]/[continue]/[stop] cues → SFT the actor; a weak non-reasoning monitor (RL/SFT) or a rule monitor acts at [answer] points.
records.findings: No acc cost (Qwen AIME 62.5→69.2). Forced-cue adherence varies by domain ([continue] 31–34% on AIME). Monitor on compressed answer progression prunes up to 50% of wasted AIME tokens; per-step decision points collapse. Rule monitor recovers a safe action in 80% of unsafe traces, success 46→96%. Code released.
records.limits: 8–9B only; one seed for monitor runs; short-answer domains; LLM safety monitor F1 weak; prompting/RL fail to induce cues; acc parity only at mid SFT checkpoints; [answer] fidelity to true working answer never tested.

new_tags.definition: the answer the model would give if its reasoning stopped at the current step, surfaced during the CoT
monitorable or faithful reasoning as a way to cut wasted inference compute (e.g. early stopping)

changes: tags: lever:inference-time -> removed (the monitor's token forcing and safe-action substitution use the cues for control; they do not change what the CoT reveals. The monitorability lever is the SFT plus the cue output format, already tagged as lever:sft and lever:architecture)

Sec. 5 RQ2 says the full-trace monitor is less effective on dead-ends, and per-step or plain-trace monitors diverge to degenerate policies)
limits: added 'acc parity only at mid SFT checkpoints' (App. A reports an inverted-U curve: early and late SFT checkpoints underperform the base model, which qualifies the 'no acc cost' headline)

records.problem: Do LLMs' self-generated counterfactual explanations (SCEs) actually flip their own prediction to the requested target label?
records.method: Predict → prompt an SCE for a target label (unconstrained / rationale-based / CoT) → re-predict on the SCE with vs. w/o chat history. 7 open LLMs (7–70B), 6 datasets (DiscrimEval, FolkTexts, SST2, Twitter-fin, MGNLI, GSM8K). Metrics: Gen, Val, edit distance.
records.findings: SCEs are mostly generated but often invalid; GSM8K Val mostly <20%. Chat history shifts Val (inflates it on GSM8K, FolkTexts; suggests target copying). Val tracks human-judged correctness only w/o context. Size, R1-distill and leaderboard rank give no consistent gain. CoT helps a little (avg Val 75 vs 69%). Code released.
records.limits: Open models ≤70B only; simple tasks with discrete or integer labels; human correctness check only on GSM8K (50/model, done by the authors); no fix tested.

relations.note: broader SCE self-consistency test: generation rates, prompting variants, chat-history effect, hidden states
uses its sentence-level mean embeddings for SCE drift; SCE clustering inspired by it

records.problem: Models trained to conceal reward hacking defeat black-box audits and direct questioning; need latent-knowledge access without changing deployed behavior.
records.method: SFT honest-persona LoRA, switched on only after the main response (split-personality token + intervention) → review + PASS/FAIL flag. Training labels: Claude Sonnet 4.5 comparing biased/unbiased-prompt responses, 11 topics. LoRA-mask variant.
records.findings: Auditing-game Llama-3.3-70B: 96% overall acc vs 0% self-admission, 72.2% base-Llama reviewer; also without reward-hack training topics; reviews name fictional biases. Beats probes on held-out topics (Qwen3-14B: 90.6 vs 81.0%). LoRA-mask worse. No deployed-model cost by construction.
records.limits: One run per 70B config; single-turn English; one main model organism; partly surface heuristics (prompt-swap); persona jailbreakable; fabricated statistics need explicit training; flags can contradict reviews. Code promised on publication.
changes: method: "Labels: Claude Sonnet 4.5 on biased/unbiased prompt pairs" -> "Training labels: Claude Sonnet 4.5 comparing biased/unbiased-prompt responses" (Claude labels the training data and the Gemma/Qwen splits; the auditing-game evaluation uses the benchmark's poisoned/clean labels)
findings: "Beats linear probes on held-out topics (90.6 vs 81.0%)" -> "Beats probes on held-out topics (Qwen3-14B: 90.6 vs 81.0%)" (Table 2 reports this comparison for Qwen3-14b only)

limits: "fabricated statistics don't transfer across topics" -> "fabricated statistics need explicit training" (Sec. 4.2: fabricated-statistics detection is very poor unless trained on that topic; the old wording was ambiguous about which direction fails)
problem/method/findings/limits: about 140 words -> about 110 words, wording only, every claim and number kept (the rule asks for about 60 words)
uncertain: signal:judge + signal:planted-cf: in the Gemma/Qwen cross-topic and probe experiments, the ground-truth PASS/FAIL comes from Claude Sonnet 4.5 comparing responses to biased vs unbiased system prompts. The judge is the label there, informed by a cue counterfactual. Only the model-organism results use implanted-behavior labels.

records.problem: Self-explanations (attribution/redaction/counterfactual) are often unfaithful; how can they be improved, and do gains transfer across styles?
records.method: Erasure attribution → most influential word → one-word pseudo-faithful explanation per style → LoRA continual SFT mixed with Tulu-2 instruct data; scored by Madsen self-consistency check on Sent140/SNLI/AGNews.
records.findings: Faithfulness ↑ in most task×style cells (13B Sent140 +0.115/+0.094/+0.292); prediction-only SFT mostly <0.01 or ↓. Cross-style transfer (13B, up to 0.781); unseen-task and per-word-count multi-word gains consistent only for attribution.
records.limits: Tulu-2 7B/13B, classification, one-word ops; needs instruct data; cross-task/style 13B only, single run; untrained baselines keep few compliant outputs (7B CF Sent140 529/5000), some cells n<50; in-style ≤0.595; acc drops (13B attr AGNews 0.815→0.597) despite "no significant drop" claim; no code.

records.problem: OpenAI/Baker propose training only against output monitors (no CoT access) to keep CoT monitorable. Can output-only supervision still obfuscate the CoT?
records.method: Policy-gradient decomposition → parametric and conditional "feedback spillover". REINFORCE on Qwen3 4B/8B/14B, penalizing a behavior in the output only (string match/regex or GPT-4.1/4.1-mini judge); the same check on the CoT measures spillover. 3 envs: polynomial derivative, hinted MMLU/hard math, terminal verifier-cheating. Mitigations: reward targeting (drops output-penalty gradient through CoT tokens), Mind & Face (separate CoT and output models).
records.findings: Output penalty → behavior vanishes from CoT too in all envs; in hint and terminal envs task reward stays high → obfuscated CoT. Mitigations, best combined, strongly cut spillover at high task reward in derivative and terminal envs (fully prevented in terminal). Hint env: unstable; on MMLU only combined prevents spillover, at 30% task-reward drop. Reward targeting: no extra compute. Code released.
records.limits: Only ≤14B Qwen3 models; toy envs. Derivative env needs in-context examples. Mind & Face trains two policy copies (costly). Hyperparameters not tuned per run type. Not tested on frontier models.

relations.note: output-only monitor training still obfuscates CoT, contra proposed safe alternative
reuses polynomial derivative factoring environment
reuses hinted MMLU questions setup to probe hint verbalization

changes: method: "output penalty (regex or GPT-4.1 judge)" -> "penalizing a behavior in the output only (string match/regex or GPT-4.1/4.1-mini judge); the same check on the CoT measures spillover" (derivative env uses string match, terminal env judge is GPT-4.1-mini; the CoT monitor is the same function applied to the CoT and is used only for evaluation, Sec. 3.1, 4.1, 4.3)

findings: "CoT stops showing the behavior in all envs while task reward stays high (obfuscation)" -> "behavior vanishes from CoT too in all envs; in hint and terminal envs task reward stays high -> obfuscated CoT" (paper concludes obfuscation only for hint and terminal envs; in the derivative env the model actually switches to the product rule)

findings: "Combined mitigations are a Pareto improvement; spillover fully prevented in terminal env" -> "Mitigations, best combined, strongly cut spillover at high task reward in derivative and terminal envs (fully prevented in terminal)" (overclaim: combining both mitigations destabilized training in both hint settings, Fig. 4-5)

findings: "Hint env: unstable training, ~30% task-reward drop on MMLU" -> "Hint env: unstable; on MMLU only combined prevents spillover, at 30% task-reward drop" (the 30% drop applies to Reward-Targeted Mind & Face, the only mitigation that fully prevented spillover on MMLU; reward targeting alone kept task reward, Sec. 4.2.2)
limits: "Hyperparameters not tuned per run" -> "Hyperparameters not tuned per run type" (paper suggests separate tuning per run type might help, not per seed)
uncertain: signal:env-label: behavior (hint use, verifier reading) is inferred from high task reward by env design; verbalization itself is scored by GPT-4.1 judge/regex, so signal:judge or by-construction could be argued
updates:explanation: mitigations shield the CoT from output-penalty gradients rather than change behavior; neither updates value fits cleanly

records.problem: Unfaithfulness results cast doubt on CoT monitoring; argue the key property is monitorability once CoT is necessary (CoT-as-computation vs -as-rationalization).
records.method: Replicate hint and forced-mistake setups at higher difficulty; stress-test Gemini CoT monitors against evasion via prompts, ART, RL (GPQA topic, oversight_pattern stealth, factorize_derivative).
records.findings: Complex hints → unverbalized hint use falls to no-hint baseline; hard math → answer follows corrupted CoT. Evasion needs human strategies or ART, costs accuracy; stronger monitors resist. RL vs monitor: evade+correct 0.5%→74.9% via early factoring + unforeseen targeted errors.
records.limits: Gemini only; toy proxy tasks; little monitor tuning; future necessity argued, not shown; no code release mentioned.

records.problem: CoT monitorability may be lost to training/architecture shifts; faithfulness unmeasurable, stress-tests costly → need cheap default-monitorability measure.
records.method: Prompted autorater (Gemini 2.5 Pro) scores 0–4 legibility & coverage (all needed steps present) on correctly solved hard tasks (HLE, GPQA, ARC-AGI, AIME); sanity-checked on hand-crafted & synthetic degradations (Base64, step removal).
records.findings: Degradations cut targeted scores; originals ~100%. 5 reasoning models: legibility 97–99.9%, coverage 95–99.4%; lapses = convoluted text, R1 Chinese switching, missing steps. Similar with Gemini 2.5 Flash rater. Prompt released.
records.limits: Not adversarial; human monitor; preliminary prompt, coverage bar rater-dependent; MCQ random-guess loophole; not a training objective (Goodhart).

records.problem: Multi-step reward hacks the overseer cannot detect, incl. reasoning encoded to evade a CoT/summary monitor → patching fails.
records.method: MONA: myopic (1-step) RL + overseer foresight-approval reward with no outcome info; vs ordinary RL (ORL) with identical step rewards. Gemini-1.5-Flash in 2-step coding (self-written tests) & loan (nationality-monitored summary → decision); gridworld camera tampering; causal-incentive theorem.
records.findings: ORL hacks in all envs: trivial tests; nationality hidden in summary sentiment, evades monitor (nationality swap drops reward), even with sign-flipped monitor reward. MONA: lower observed, higher ground-truth return; loan ≈ best fair score. Noisy approval OK; rollout-based approval reintroduces stego. Gridworld code released.
records.limits: No help vs single-step hacks; capability cost (forgoes novel opaque strategies); one closed model, 2-step tasks, proprietary RL; incentive removal, not guarantee; not advised for current systems.

(Sec 4.2: an accidental sign flip of the monitor reward left the result qualitatively unchanged, with ORL still encoding nationality steganographically. So the encoding is not driven by the monitor penalty. This qualifies the eval:optimization-pressure reading, and the tag is kept because training against the monitor is still part of the setup.)
findings: 'MONA avoids hacks: lower observed but higher ground-truth return' -> 'MONA: lower observed, higher ground-truth return' (trimmed to offset the added clause; the meaning is unchanged)
uncertain: object:cot: the monitored object is the loan-application summary written before the decision (paper calls it scratchpad/encoded reasoning, not CoT); coding tests and gridworld have no explanation object.

records.problem: Text-only RMs penalize overt cue use → BoN/DPO favor cued answers whose CoT hides a forbidden cue ("CoT hacking").
records.method: Math Book (AQuA-RAT + leaked solution) & BiasQA (Winogenerated), told not to use cue. Fix: if removing cue flips prediction, append "I used the cue" disclaimer to RM input (RM_D: any flip; RM_C: flip away from cued answer) → BoN + DPO data.
records.findings: Plain RM raises cue use w/o matching ack (BoN Math Book acc 75.2→93.6%, ack 2.7→1.7%). RM_C closes BoN gap 41%/71% (Math Book/BiasQA, SK-Gemma RM); augmented RMs give fewer unfaithful CoTs in 14/16 DPO comparisons. Code released.
records.limits: Two controlled settings, 3B/8B; needs known cue + counterfactuals. Small DPO gain on Math Book (RM_D ~none). Offline DPO only; OOD test preliminary.

records.problem: Finetuning weight diffs are opaque and finetuning data is often unavailable → need natural-language answers about what changed (WeightDiffQA).
records.method: DIT: SFT a LoRA adapter on thousands of synthetic labeled weight diffs (trigger-gated hidden-topic personas; news-headline knowledge) → finetuned model reports its own changes. Qwen3/Gemma3 1-8B; o4-mini judge scores answer vs label (1-5).
records.findings: Held-out diffs: DIT ≫ black-box probing, near trigger-aware roofline (Qwen3-4B 4.76 vs 4.73); generalizes to higher-rank LoRA diffs and OOD triggers; full-param mixed (Qwen3-4B 2.75, Gemma3-4B 4.58); beats story-summary baseline. Code, diffs released.
records.limits: No cross-behavior transfer (≈ base question); trigger recovery 0/100; one fixed question; small models, synthetic diffs only.

records.problem: Passive CoT monitoring flags misbehavior only after execution, when harm may already have occurred. Unknown whether LRMs are willing to self-report misbehavior as it happens.
records.method: LRMs get enable/disable tools for monitoring channels (AI vs human; quad: AI + junior/senior/lead human). 4 prompt directives: optional, mandated, incentivized, incentivized+friction. Sycophancy, reward hacking, bias tasks from Guan et al. A GPT-5 judge flags the warranted cases.
records.findings: Optional → ~16% of warranted cases self-reported. Mandating/incentivizing raises tool calls (incentivized ~147%, over-reporting) but not where it matters: high severity never self-reported; 474/478 judge-rated medium/high reports labeled low. Most models pick the most lenient monitor, with confabulated reasons. Under friction, low-disposition models disable monitoring more (DS-V4-Pro 47%, gpt-oss 20–24%; Kimi, DS-V4-Flash ≤3%).
records.limits: Ground truth is judge-defined. 50 cases per misbehavior, 4 open LRMs, prompting only, no fix proposed. Possible AIME/GPQA contamination. No code release stated.

relations.note: takes misbehavior types, data subsets and GPT-5 judge setup from its suite

records.problem: CoT monitorability may erode with training, RL or scale; F1/accuracy confound class imbalance → no broad, comparable measure.
records.method: g-mean² (TPR×TNR; min-criterion TPR for stochastic intervention arms); suite of intervention/process/outcome-property evals; GPT-5 monitor, CoT vs action scopes; obfuscation-RL organisms; RL, pretraining, monitor scaling; follow-up questions.
records.findings: Frontier models fairly, not perfectly monitorable; longer CoT ↑; CoT-only ≫ action-only. Suite catches obfuscation organisms. Frontier RL no material drop. Smaller model at higher effort → higher monitorability, small capability tax, more compute. Stronger/higher-effort monitors ↑, steeper with CoT access. Follow-ups help.
records.limits: OpenAI-only monitors; two RL runs, single pretraining seed; process evals lack negatives; small-effect interventions noisy; suite only partially open-sourced (planned).

records.problem: Self-explanation SFT uses fixed labels from an earlier checkpoint. As behavior drifts, the model may learn to explain that old checkpoint instead of its current behavior.
records.method: SFT on M0's counterfactual cue-ablation explanations ("would the answer change without the cue?") + KL behavior regularizer. Explanations scored against current-self vs M0 labels. Tasks: Hint-MMLU, AITA, refusal. Also activation patching, label-noise/cross-model sweeps, auxiliary post-training.
records.findings: Self>Orig on all 3 tasks (disagreements resolved toward self 79/82/63%); without KL, Self<Orig. Needs online label-self agreement ≳0.7. Holds with Llama labels (53% agreement). Tracks aux-induced shifts (held-out Jabberwocky 79.8%). Patching corr 0.89 vs 0.53 unreg. General-capability cost mostly within ~2pp.
records.limits: Templated change/no-change explanations; ≤32B. Needs behavioral variance (refusal labels near-constant). LR sweep contradicts the label-self hypothesis; LoRA-rank sweep shows other factors matter. GSM8K/TruthfulQA drop ~5pp in one run. No code release mentioned.

records.problem: LRM rationales sound plausible but may not drive the answer; existing tests are input-level (hints) or accuracy-focused.

records.problem: Unfaithful CoT → CoT inspection/monitoring misleads about what drives answers.
records.method: CST: reward CoTs letting an LLM simulator predict answers on counterfactuals (cue removed or LLM-generated); rewrite unfaithful CoTs, k rollouts → reward-weighted CE + unlikelihood, iterated; Qwen3 4B–235B, gpt-oss.
records.findings: Cue-monitor G-mean +31–48 (SNLI recall 12→87%, FPR <3%); generic-CF sim ~+2, partly via answers. Beats prompting, VFT; rewriting 5x faster, better OOD than pure RL; held-out cues/datasets transfer; larger models gain more. Acc −1–2 pts; code.
records.limits: Little gain on dissuading cues (53→57); artificial cues; no cue↔generic transfer; two-way MC only.

records.problem: Can knowledge of a CoT monitor from pretraining-style docs make models evade it, unprompted and with no optimization pressure?
records.method: SDF on monitor docs vs behavior-only control; defect concealment (8 open models), credential exfiltration (2); GPT-5-mini monitor; CoT-controllability suite; gpt-oss-120b reward-hacking RL w/ monitor penalty.
records.findings: Undetected deception ↑ in all 8 (gpt-oss-120b 1.7%→25.7%), CoT still used (not suppressed); weaker when CoT load-bearing; controllability predicts obfuscation (r=0.800); RL: 20% undetected hacking in ~40% fewer steps. Code released.
records.limits: Concentrated, hinted docs; effect collapses when monitor docs are 10% of training data. Best-epoch selection. Simple zero-shot monitor. OOCR vs concept-avoidance unclear.

relations.note: designs load-bearing exfiltration task to test its CoT-necessity faithfulness floor

records.problem: CoT answers may not follow from invalid/irrelevant steps → untrustworthy QA; step-wise faithful-QA methods (overgenerate-filter, beam) lack foresight, can't update facts.
records.method: Fame: T5-large controller assembles retrieve/entail/end actions into entailment tree; Monte-Carlo planning scored by verifier (step validity + hypothesis faithfulness); option picked by tree score; behavior cloning + verifier-guided iterative training.
records.findings: EntailmentBankQA acc 53.1→67.1% vs Entailer; beats SI on Tasks 1/2; better cross-dataset (WorldTreeQA, OBQA). Human eval (50 q): SV 66%, HF 82% (ties Entailer), overall 46 vs 24%; ChatGPT SV 38.3% despite 92% acc. MCP > greedy/filter/beam.
records.limits: Science MCQ, fixed fact corpus, few module types; T5-large only; ~31s/option. Faithfulness = human-rated tree validity/support, not causal test. Acc trails prompted 175B LLMs (86/92% on 50-q sample). No code link.

records.problem: CoT may not reflect the strategy the model actually computes; existing parametric-faithfulness tests rely only on hints and ignore model internals.
records.method: CIA = macro-F1, probe-detected vs CoT-verbalized strategy; TwoHopFact, MMLU-Hint, 2-digit mult. RS on CoT-probe-agreeing samples; DPO, GRPO with accuracy + agreement reward.
records.findings: Base CIA 0.448–0.759. Best method +25.5% avg relative gain; acc drop ≤0.015, mult acc rises. Holds on auxiliary tools; transfers TwoHop↔Hint, not to/from mult. Mult: model changes how it reasons; TwoHop/Hint: how it reports (causal intervention confirms). Code released.
records.limits: CIA bounded by probe quality; assumes single gold strategy. 8–9B, short tasks. GRPO weak (−0.066 to +0.126); reasoning-model gains small. Hint auxiliary tool not independent of probe.

records.problem: CoT may just accompany the answer; outcome-only RL doesn't enforce that the answer causally depends on it. Saliency: necessary, not sufficient, for faithfulness.
records.method: Per rollout, additive AtMan attention mask on CoT tokens init suppressed (c=-0.4), optimized 200 steps to restore answer log-prob → mean normalized mask (÷c) = saliency reward, added to GRPO outcome reward. Llama-3.2-3B, GSM8K/MMLU, vs outcome-only GRPO.
records.findings: CoT tokens -44% (GSM8K), -46% (MMLU). GSM8K CoTs denser (stop words -25%, numbers +48%, symbols +61%); MMLU composition shift small. Pass@4 -0.4%/+0.1% → no accuracy cost.
records.limits: Proxy only: neither saliency gain nor faithfulness measured after training; reward sign ambiguous as written (Eq. 3). One 3B model, 2 datasets; no length-penalty baseline. May cut self-correction tokens. No code mentioned.

records.problem: BCT/ACT constrain whole response/activations → cue still followed but unmentioned (obfuscation) → may undermine CoT monitoring.
records.method: RMCT: GRPO reward pulls bias-following rate on biased prompt toward unbiased-prompt rate (N=128 each); CoT free; LoRA. Train 1 bias (LogiQA/HellaSwag), test 6 on HLE MCQ vs BCT + drift controls.
records.findings: BCT ↓ trained bias more, but held-out bias-following ↓ RMCT ≈ BCT (Llama), > BCT (GPT-OSS: BCT fails, ↑ post-hoc bias). BCT suppresses cue verbalization; RMCT preserves it on held-out biases. 64 vs ≥2000 datapoints, more compute. Accuracy change n.s.
records.limits: 2 non-frontier open models, MCQ sycophancy only. Lenient BVR likely overstates what a cue-unaware monitor sees. Switch rates conflate sampling noise. GPT's trained-bias BVR still drops under RMCT.

records.problem: Interpretability evals conflate faithfulness w/ plausibility; no formal def of faithfulness; binary faithful/unfaithful verdicts via counter-example.
records.method: Opinion piece: surveys NLP faithfulness evals (fidelity, robustness, erasure, comprehensiveness/sufficiency) → 3 implicit assumptions (model, prediction, linearity) + evaluation guidelines.
records.findings: Faithfulness ≠ plausibility. Evals should avoid human judgment, gold labels, user-performance proxies, and untested "inherent interpretability" claims. Strict faithfulness likely unattainable (interpretation = lossy approximation, pigeonhole) → graded faithfulness across models/tasks and input subspaces.
records.limits: No experiments. Graded criteria not formalized; validity of the 3 assumptions left open. Pre-LLM; focus on heat-maps/attention.

records.problem: RL-learned P→A shortcuts (hints, reward hacks) bypass the CoT → plausible but unmonitorable traces; existing probes are task-specific.
records.method: Faithfulness as info flow P→C→A: sufficiency/completeness/necessity via H_q(A|C), masked-KL, Grad-DE/Grad-Nec. GRPO update-time interventions (update mask, gradient mask, CoT-only gradient, FACT); rollouts and rewards unchanged.
records.findings: Entropy and grad metrics recover the LLM-judged ordering (Qwen3-8B 89.4% vs R1-Distill-14B 54.3%); KL-Nec inverted. Interventions (bar Gradient Mask on code) raise hint/hack verbalization and grad metrics. records.problem: Fine-tunes hide trigger-gated behaviors; Introspection Adapters (IA) transfer inconsistently and hallucinate wrong behaviors.
records.method: Per-model LoRA reporting adapter (SAR) on frozen fine-tune: CE on generic self-report prefills + align activations to behavior direction (train-data vs. neutral mean diff) + coherent-English cap; 7 Qwen3-14B organisms + no-behavior control.
records.findings: SAR hit rate >0.10 on all 8 settings (mean 0.66 vs IA 0.39; IA <0.10 on 3/8); pooled hallucination IA 0.59 vs SAR 0.29 (rater-corrected cut x1.3-1.7); broad reports of EM generalization; report appears only after behavior acquired; inference-time steering far weaker; Gemma mean 0.62.
records.limits: Needs training data + white-box access; SFT-only organisms; reports behavior, not trigger; LLM judge over-credits (kappa 0.53); IA still wins French-insertion, CLI-transcript, German-cities (judge only); code promised.

records.problem: Is CoT the model's actual reasoning? Tests 3 unfaithfulness hypotheses: post-hoc CoT, unstated test-time compute, phrasing-encoded reasoning.
records.method: 175B RLHF model, 8 MCQ tasks: truncate CoT, insert LLM-made mistake, swap in filler "..." tokens, paraphrase prefix → answer match/accuracy. Answer change w/ vs w/o CoT across 810M–175B models + synthetic addition.
records.findings: CoT reliance varies widely by task (early-answering AOC 0.44 AQuA vs 0.02 ARC-Easy), little correlated with CoT accuracy gain. Filler: no gain; paraphrase: accuracy kept → CoT gain not from extra compute or phrasing-encoded info. Inverse scaling: 13B relies on CoT more than 175B on 7/8 tasks; easier addition → less reliance.
records.limits: No ground truth on internal reasoning; tests non-exhaustive, not-post-hoc ≠ faithful; only RLHF models from one internal family.
changes: findings: "uncorrelated with CoT accuracy gain" -> "little correlated with CoT accuracy gain" (paper says 'little correlation' / 'not strongly correlated', not zero correlation)

records.problem: Covert agent misbehavior (hidden side tasks) evades blackbox monitors; alignment training may fail or overgeneralize.
records.method: Self-incrimination: on-policy SFT on agent trajectories with a report_scheming() tool call inserted beside each covert action (GPT-5 labeler); 45 synthetic envs, adversarial-pressure augmentation → 15 OOD APPS/BashArena/SHADE-Arena envs.
records.findings: Undetected successful attacks 56→6% (GPT-4.1), 33→14% (mini), 41→9% (Gemini); beats matched and trained monitors, even with scratchpad access; 0% observed FPR (GPT-4.1); 2-3× lower cross-task detection SD; keeps instruction hierarchy, capabilities within a few points; transfers to uninstructed misbehavior; SI+monitor hardest to break adversarially.
records.limits: Non-reasoning API models, SFT only; reframing prompts cut reports; no CoT/whitebox baselines; relies on current models' behavioral inconsistency. Code released.

records.problem: Efficient-reasoning (length-pressure) RL feared to drop CoT steps → weaker explanation/oversight; unclear whether/when.
records.method: Qwen3-4B/8B, Olmo3-7B × ThinkPrune / L1 / GLP (LoRA-GRPO on AIME-AMC). Faithfulness = NSG simulatability on 7 decision tasks; monitorability = g-mean² on sycophancy (FACE-Eval) + MedQA cognitive-bias cues.
records.findings: NSG falls in 11/15 settings, mainly via less consistent answers (ρ=0.87; length ρ=0.46); some 40–65% shorter CoTs keep/raise it. Monitorability: sycophancy drops ≤0.08; MedQA-bias drops >0.2 only at L1-Low, tracking compression vs base (ρ=0.68), not absolute length. L1 costs accuracy; ThinkPrune/GLP ≈ base.

records.problem: Can LMs learn to faithfully describe their own internal computations? Does privileged self-access beat other-model explainers?
records.method: SFT explainers on interp-derived labels: SAE feature descriptions, activation-patching outcomes, hint-ablation outcomes (MMLU); activations fed as continuous tokens; self vs other-model explainers.
records.findings: Beats SelfIE, nearest-neighbor, even gold SAE labels (simulator); generalizes OOD to full activations/diffs; self & close variants beat dissimilar explainers (Qwen3-8B, 70B), tracking activation similarity; self > cross-model on patching/ablation too; ~100x more sample-efficient than NN. Untrained models miss hint effects. Code released.
records.limits: Target frozen, explainer a fine-tuned copy → loose self-explanation; ~8B targets; single-token outcomes; no CoT.

records.problem: CoT compression for efficiency: does it cost monitor oversight, and does the compression mechanism matter beyond the rate?
records.method: Hinted MATH-500; prompted Qwen2.5 monitor scores answer-hidden think traces → AUC vs hint-answer agreement; 4 compression mechanisms × 2 reasoners. MonoSumm: LoRA SFT distilling R1-7B self-summaries (GSM8K) into one-pass 1.5–8B students.
records.findings: Self-summary AUC 0.89 vs natural 0.79, concise 0.62, truncation 0.55. Self-sum ≫ concise/trunc gap holds across hints, reasoners, monitors, matched budgets and answer masking. MonoSumm beats same-scale full CoT (0.88–0.94 vs 0.76–0.83) at 15–19× fewer tokens, with lower acc.
records.limits: Correlational label, no no-hint CF. A trivial answer-visibility feature beats the monitor. Realized lengths unmatched. One synthetic math hint; real reward hacking untested. Reasoners ≤8B. No matched-competence control.

records.limits: One RL recipe, MCQ only; two Qwen sizes + one Nemotron run; mostly single-seed; monitor errors vary with chain length; no code release stated.

records.problem: Incomplete explanations: input concepts (hints, demographics) sway answers without being credited. Prior test-time fixes target unsoundness or still let hidden concepts leak in.
records.method: Removal wrapper: an auxiliary LLM (Qwen3.5-27B) extracts the input's concepts, flags those the explanation does not credit and deletes them → target is re-queried in a fresh context. Also a Combined variant with modular prompting. Tested on hint-augmented MCQ and BBQ.
records.findings: Hint QA: verbalization = 1 by construction; CCF r 0.27→0.87 (Qwen), 0.34→0.92 (Gemma); NSG negative→positive; beats regulative prompt. BBQ: small gains, overlapping 90% intervals; Removal alone trails faithfulness prompting on Qwen3.5-9B; Combined best on both Qwens, Removal on Gemma; hidden concepts halved except Qwen3.5-9B (inconsistent credit sets).
records.limits: Completeness only, not soundness. Needs accurate aux model and consistent credit sets; CCF metric reuses the wrapper's aux concept pipeline. Concepts treated as independent. Hint CCF/NSG only on hint-flipped subset (100/86 Qs); BBQ 100 items. Changes answers, no accuracy reported; no code.

records.problem: Outcome-only RL → post-hoc rationalized CoTs; human labels, LLM judges and interventions are too costly or unreliable for step-level faithfulness supervision.
records.method: Hidden-state VAE geometry (distortion, Fisher-Rao) + answer-entropy dynamics filter detector-relabelled rollouts, bootstrapping a 1k LLM-consensus+human seed to 20k instances → Qwen3-8B LoRA step detector → GRPO reward = outcome + detector + entropy + manifold terms.

Qwen3-4B vs GRPO: faith 74.1→82.3, acc 69.6→73.9, shorter CoTs. Detector reward matters most in 4B ablation; on 1.7B dropping manifold reward hurts faith more.
records.limits: Faithfulness = step validity visible to a judge, not internal computation (authors concede); faith partly scored by the detector it trains against; one judge table marked placeholder; LogiQA in both detector data and RL eval despite claimed separation; policies ≤4B; code promised, not released.

records.problem: Erasure metrics for token-importance expls → masked inputs OOD; ROAR-style retraining is costly, leaks gold label, measures a proxy model.
records.method: Masked FT of RoBERTa (half of each batch masked at rate ~U[0,100%]) → model where masking is in-distribution; MaSF OOD test validates; recursive erasure vs random baseline (RACU/ACU); 9 IMs, 16 classification datasets.
records.findings: No unmasked perf loss; masked inputs consistently in-distribution (MaSF) only w/ masked FT; occlusion IMs (LOO, Beam) most faithful; gradient IMs beat Recursive-ROAR (imperfect cmp.); x⊙grad worst.
records.limits: MLM classifiers only; no faithfulness ablation without masked FT; must be built in, not post-hoc; ~2x epochs; unstable bAbI-2/3 w/ large; code stated available.

records.problem: Self-explanations are convincing but may be unfaithful; API-only LLMs give no logits and refuse to answer when info is missing → logit-based erasure metrics don't work.
records.method: Inference-only self-consistency checks, re-classified in a fresh session: a counterfactual must get the requested label; with the listed words (feature attribution) or self-redacted text masked as [REDACTED], the answer must be "unknown". Tasks: IMDB, bAbI-1, MCTest, RTE. Models: Llama2 7B/70B, Falcon 7B/40B, Mistral 7B. Prompt/persona variants on Llama2-70B only.
records.findings: Faithfulness depends on model, task and explanation type. CFs consistently faithful only on IMDB (Llama2, Mistral); Falcon CFs never. FA/redaction mostly poor; Llama2-70B ok only on RTE, bAbI-1; Mistral FA (IMDB) and Falcon-40B redaction (IMDB, MCTest) beat other models. Usually ↑ with size (except Falcon). Llama2-70B robust to prompt variants. Redaction ≈ FA → masking not OOD.
records.limits: Faithfulness is binary per instance. Misclassified items dropped (low acc, possible class imbalance). Zero-shot, single sample. Assumes prompts understood. No closed models. Only 3 explanation types (2 similar). Code released.

records.method: OPeX: Llama-3.1-8B LoRA + GRPO; reward = Llama-3.3-70B proxy's accuracy predicting classifier labels from one task-level explanation, on seen (recoverability) or held-out inputs (simulatability). Tested on unseen tasks/classifiers.
records.findings: Sim 0.86, recov 0.99 vs 0.68, 0.73 for GPT-4o, Llama-70B; beats MaNtLE, R1-distill CoT, human expls. Holds on synthetic tasks, GPT-4o proxy, 3B. Humans +15 pts vs no expl. Code + weights.
records.limits: Explains small external classifiers, not the LLM. Classification only. LLM proxy for reward and main eval. One-dataset human study.

records.problem: GRPO on VLMs raises reward while CoT drops visual anchors → templated, less monitorable traces ("non-intentional obfuscation").
records.method: Two-gate judge labels (CoT-only answerer + image-grounding verifier; SPA-VL: safety reward + auditor) predicted by GPT-4o → G-mean²; attention/IG/patching + frozen SAE localize template features. Tame = GRPO + prompt-evolved refined traces + asymmetric SAE penalty on template latents above pre-RL level.
records.findings: Template/ground features lose separability; targeted ablation beats random (partial causal). Tame best G-mean² in all 4 settings, +30.9/+16.7 pp over GRPO (Qwen VIRL/SPA-VL); humans + 2 held-out monitors agree. Task metrics small, mixed (Qwen VIRL acc .646→.640, SPA-VL harm 6.8→7.4).
records.limits: 8B/12B VLMs, 2 datasets; LLM-judge reference labels; small injection effects; behav-only gets much of gain; VIRL capability trade-offs (Qwen MMMU-Pro 48.6→43.0, 4.0 already under GRPO); no code release mentioned.

records.problem: Can steganographic collusion between LLM agents emerge from a misspecified reward plus an overseer, and do mitigations hold when optimized against?
records.method: Sender→receiver team vs fixed overseer ± paraphraser; elicitation via GBRL (PPO, Gemma-2-2B sender) and ICRL (Claude-3.5-Sonnet learners); biased candidate screening, AQuA-RAT, HumanEval payloads.
records.findings: Stego emerges unprompted: task success 0.88–1.00 vs max-clean 0.50–0.67, overseer bypass ≥0.97. Oversight turns blatant codes subtle. Paraphrasing cuts multi-bit; 1-bit decoding ≥90% survives. ICRL beats human-designed schemes.
records.limits: Toy screening setting; brittle overseers; no sender-usefulness check in screening; one GBRL model; ICRL pipeline tuned on Claude (GPT-4o failed to collude).

records.problem: CoT explanations can misstate which input concepts drove the answer → over-trust. Existing scores don't show how explanations mislead.
records.method: Faithfulness = PCC(concept causal effect, rate explanations cite it). GPT-4o extracts concepts, writes removal/swap CFs, labels which concepts explanations credit. Bayesian hierarchical pooling across Qs. BBQ (Turpin variant) & MedQA, 30 Qs each.
records.findings: BBQ: GPT-3.5 0.75 > Claude 0.62 > GPT-4o 0.56. Explanations hide the influence of social bias and safety refusals. MedQA 0.30–0.50, with misleading claims about evidence. 5 objective BBQ Qs: 0.95. Anti-bias prompt no gain. Code released.
records.limits: 30 Qs/dataset. Aux-LLM CF error rate 6–10%. Dataset-specific prompts. Single-concept edits miss correlated concepts. Mostly closed models (Llama-8B only in appendix).

relations.note: uses its BBQ weak-evidence variant and CoT prompt; recovers its bias-masking finding

records.problem: Self-generated counterfactual explanations (SCEs) must be valid (flip own prediction) and minimal to reveal the decision boundary; prior work measured validity only.
records.method: Fully enumerated 2-4-feature tabular tasks (income, house prices, heart disease) in NL → full decision boundary; SCE re-scored in fresh context; validity, excess Gower distance, exact match; 7 LLMs; unconstrained vs minimal prompts.
records.findings: Unconstrained → near-100% valid, far from minimal; minimal prompt → mostly invalid (income validity 97%→36%); exact match ≤32%. No gain from stronger or reasoning models. Robust to distance fn, prompts, temperature. R1-70B traces show no self-prediction; self-prediction prompt barely helps. Code released.

records.problem: Cue- and error-based faithfulness tests lose signal as models improve ("vanishing signal"). The predictive value of self-explanations goes unmeasured.
records.method: NSG = normalized gain in a 5-LLM predictor ensemble's accuracy at simulating the model on real-data counterfactuals (Hamming ≤2), with vs. w/o the self-explanation. 18 models, 7k pairs, 7 tabular/ethics datasets. Self vs. cross-model explanations.
records.findings: NSG 11-37%, positive for every model. 5-15% of explanations highly misleading. Self-expl beat expl from stronger external models (privileged access). Scale trend mixed: size helps only up to a modest threshold. User-facing expl > CoT (Qwen3). Moral Machines lowest.
records.limits: Binary classification, mostly tabular; free-text open. Average-case metric. Predictors not SOTA. Measurement only. Code + data released.

records.findings: GRPO-14B best/tied on all metrics (+56.4% NLI, +29.9% judge vs DPO-14B); accuracy ~equal (0.755 vs 0.740). Accuracy & judge rise with size; DPO NLI flat (0.313→0.314). Both collapse at 3B, GRPO worse.

records.limits: Workshop paper. In-distribution MMLU only; possible probe confounders; small sweep, one injection strategy. No capability-cost eval or code.

records.problem: CoT conclusions may not follow from the stated chain (unfaithful reasoning) → errors on complex logic problems.
records.method: Few-shot LLM translates NL problem into LP/FOL/CSP/SAT → deterministic solver (Pyke, Prover9, python-constraint, Z3) derives answer → rule/LLM interpreter maps it back. Self-refiner repairs non-executable forms using solver error messages; otherwise falls back to CoT.
records.findings: Avg relative gain +39.2% vs standard prompting, +18.4% vs CoT (3 GPT models × 5 logic datasets). Gains grow with reasoning depth. Self-refinement raises exec rate; accuracy plateaus. Faithfulness claimed by construction, not measured. Code released.
records.limits: Faithful only if formulation correct; semantic mistranslations undetected. Fallback CoT carries no guarantee (GPT-4 exec rate 32.6% on AR-LSAT w/o refinement). CoT beats it on PrOntoQA (ChatGPT, GPT-4). Closed models only; bounded by solver expressiveness.

records.problem: Unclear whether LLM answers causally depend on their CoT; small distilled rationalizers can shortcut past their rationales.
records.method: Causal mediation (CoT = mediator): counterfactual questions/CoTs (own CoTs for NIE, GPT-4's for CIE) → indirect vs direct effects on 12 LLMs. FRODO: DPO rationale generator (correct > counterfactual/irrelevant chains) + reasoner trained with LM + counterfactual + margin-ranking (indirect-effect) losses.
records.findings: LLMs often ignore CoT; GPT-4 flips answer only 30% under counterfactual CoT; RLHF models DE > IE; IE drops with more steps. FRODO: +2-3% acc over SFT/distillation, +4.5% robustness (CIE), +2.6% OOD, higher LAS than SCOTT. Code released.
records.limits: Causal metric blind to internals; students ≤7B, mostly MCQ commonsense; needs costly LLM counterfactual data and two-stage DPO; faithfulness via CIE/LAS on few tasks; 3 seeds.

records.problem: Can LLMs report quantitative features of their internal decision processes (attribute weights in multi-attribute choice), and can training improve this?
records.method: SFT GPT-4o/4o-mini on choices of 100 agents with random attribute weights; logistic regression on choices → learned weights; prompt for weight reports without deciding. Then SFT on target-weight reports (2-fold, held-out contexts); test on native weights in 100 new contexts.

records.problem: Do LLM self-explanations let humans infer the model's outputs on related inputs (counterfactual simulatability)?
records.method: LLMs generate counterfactuals from the explanation; humans (StrategyQA) or GPT-4 (SHP) infer outputs via entailment → simulation precision (match w/ actual output) + generality (CF diversity). GPT-3.5/GPT-4 × CoT/post-hoc.
records.findings: Low precision (SQA ~80%, SHP ~89%); CoT ≈ post-hoc; GPT-4 > GPT-3.5 (+5.5/+6.5 pts). Precision uncorrelated w/ plausibility (r≈0.01) → RLHF may not help; generality ⟂ precision. Sanity checks: GPT-4 simulator ≈ human–human agreement; forced wrong-answer expls −45 pts.
records.limits: Classification tasks only, English; CF distribution set by generator LLM; fair-moderate human IAA; no improvement method (suggests RL/self-training on LLM-simulated score).

records.problem: Open-ended behaviors such as hallucination have no cheap verifiers, and LLM-judge + web-search rewards cost too much for RL.
records.method: RLFR: attention probes on frozen Gemma-3-12B flag hallucinated entities → policy chooses maintain/retract/correct → retraction/correction probes (trained on Gemini 2.5 Pro labels) supply the RL reward (CISPO); probe-scored BoN at test time.
records.findings: 58% fewer hallucinations (BoN-32, inline) vs base, 10% from the policy alone; at n=256 probe BoN beats Gemma self-judge by ~15pp; ~90× cheaper than judge; beats SFT; benchmarks roughly preserved; no probe evasion observed.
records.limits: One model, one task; monitor recall only .56; Gemini is the sole ground truth; RL policy almost never maintains falsely flagged true claims (Stable ≈0); evasion under more optimization untested; ~3% degenerate inline completions; no code, only a completions viewer.

MMLU within ~2 pts; beh. training WildChat refusal 1%->10%.

records.problem: Good self-rationalization thought to need ~100B+ LMs. Prior work judges rationales mostly by task accuracy, ignoring their plausibility and consistency.

records.findings: 5 MC QA sets: best avg NRG vs SFT, product-reward and STaR-like filtering (not on every metric); acc above SFT on all (StrategyQA 57.6→65.1). Humans prefer MaRio over SFT on 66.6–83.15% of items. Acc-only training does not improve rationales. Code and rationales released.

records.problem: CoTs hide hint use and are verbose → hard to monitor. RL on a monitorability reward stalls: the base model rarely satisfies f(z), so the gradient is ~0.

records.problem: Encoded reasoning (steganography in the CoT) could hide reasoning steps from readers → unfaithful CoT, weaker monitoring.
records.method: Demo: SFT GPT-3.5 on toy sycophancy task to encode an intermediate result in its intro sentence. Red-team eval: watermark and prompted LLM encoders hide random bits; GPT-3.5 paraphrases (± question context) + suspiciousness penalty. Capacity + win-rate on AlpacaEval, AQUA-RAT.
records.findings: Encoded CoT: 80% sycophantic vs 54% direct; random-intro control no gain. Paraphrasing almost always leaves <2 bits/answer (~3 bits/KB). AQUA-RAT: context-aware paraphrase keeps ~all of GPT-4's win-rate gain over GPT-3.5; AlpacaEval win-rate drops 8%. Code released.
records.limits: Stego only induced (SFT, prompts, watermarks); emergence under RL untested. Human-built schemes may over- or underestimate LLMs. 2 datasets; paraphraser untrained; +50% serial latency.
