relations: lanham2023measuring note 'adopts its encoded-reasoning notion; extends its paraphrase test into an adversarial defense eval' -> 'takes its encoded-reasoning concept; its paraphrase-insensitivity result motivates inducing steganography' (the paper does not claim to extend Lanham's paraphrase test; it cites that result in Sec 2.2 as the reason to induce steganography; builds-on kept because this shapes the experimental design, not just related work)
uncertain: signal:known-payload is coined. signal:env-label (a program compares the decoded and original messages) or signal:by-construction might fit instead.
updates:behavior: paraphrasing removes the hidden channel, so downstream reasoning can only use the legible text. But paraphrasing literally rewrites the text, so updates:explanation is arguable.

lever:inference-time: the paper says 'We do not make the model generations more faithful through paraphrasing'. It evaluates paraphrasing as a defense rather than deploying it, so it could be read as a measurement paper with no lever.
contribution:method: the headline claim is the 'key ingredients' of paraphrasing (context-aware paraphrasing, a suspiciousness penalty) rather than a clearly new method.
contribution:benchmark rests mainly on the released repo's name (Text-Steganography-Benchmark) and the eval protocol; contribution:metric alone may be enough.
scale:small: Llama2-7B-Chat appears only as the logit-access encoder for the watermark schemes; its outputs are paraphrased but never trained.
reveals:misbehavior is omitted. In the demo, encoded reasoning hides sycophancy ('while not looking sycophantic'), which might count as misbehavior a monitor should catch.
domain:chat for AlpacaEval single-turn instruction following; domain:mcq is omitted for the sycophancy demo's two-option political questions, which are tagged domain:synthetic.
The builds-on lanham2023measuring relation: it is cited in the intro and background for the encoded-reasoning concept and its paraphrase-insensitivity finding, so it may count as related work only.

records.problem: Single-model proof+inference generators (ProofWriter) see the whole theory → inference may use premises beyond the stated proof → proofs possibly unfaithful.
records.method: FaiRR: RoBERTa-large rule selector → fact selector → T5-large composer that sees only the selected premises, iterated; the proof is a by-product of the selections; each module SFT'd on decomposed ProofWriter data.
records.findings: ≈PW-Iter on D0-D3 (EA 99.2 vs 99.8, small cost); more robust to subject perturbations (consistency 96.4 vs 87.6); 3.5× faster; errors localizable to a module; manual ablation: PW errs once irrelevant premises are added back. Code released.
records.limits: Synthetic rulebases, small models; early-stop errors → weaker on unseen depths (-3% proof acc vs PW-Iter on D5); slightly worse than PW-Iter on attribute perturbations; poor zero-shot on ParaRules.
changes: tags: metric:proof-accuracy -> removed (strict exact match to the gold proof plus a correct label, so it measures correctness, not faithfulness; FaiRR's faithfulness is by construction and never measured)
tags: metric:perturbation-consistency -> removed (the paper defines consistency as an auxiliary robustness metric, prediction invariance under subject/attribute renaming, not a faithfulness metric)

findings: 'more robust to subject perturbations (avg consistency 95.9 vs 92.9)' -> 'more robust to subject perturbations (consistency 96.4 vs 87.6)' (95.9 vs 92.9 is the average over all three perturbation sets, Table 2; the subject-only value is 96.4 vs 87.6)

findings: 'PW fails at select-then-reason once irrelevant facts are added' -> 'manual ablation: PW errs once irrelevant premises are added back' (Sec 5.5 is a small manual case study on theories already chosen because PW erred, so the record now says so)

limits: 'no gain on attribute perturbations' -> 'slightly worse than PW-Iter on attribute perturbations' (Table 2/9: EA 96.7 vs 97.8, PA 95.6 vs 97.4, C 96.5 vs 97.4; App. D: 'in attribute robustness our model performs worse')
uncertain: lever:sft and lever:prompt-pipeline: the core lever is the modular, input-restricted architecture. The modules are trained by standard SFT on decomposed data, and the pipeline uses trained modules, not prompting.
updates:behavior: in a by-construction pipeline both sides change. Chose behavior because the inference is restricted to the stated premises.
signal:generic-cf: this rests only on a small manual input-ablation case study of the ProofWriter baseline (Sec 5.5). FaiRR's own faithfulness is purely by construction.
reveals:cot-reliance vs reveals:decision-factors: the paper claims both (inference uses only the selected premises; entailment is grounded in the proofs). One may be redundant.
domain:synthetic: the D* rulebases are synthetic with gold proofs, but domain:logic is the primary fit.
metric:proof-accuracy / metric:perturbation-consistency: these are the paper's main metrics, but they measure correctness and robustness, not faithfulness itself.
contribution:benchmark omitted: the paper builds subject/attribute robustness datasets, but the abstract does not present them as a headline contribution.
Relations empty: the baselines ProofWriter, RuleTaker and PRover are not in the corpus. jacovi2020towards is cited only in related work.

records.problem: RL pressure from CoT monitors feared to drive encoded reasoning → monitoring fails.
records.method: GRPO on gpt-oss-20b/120b: Game24 + hidden side task (multiplication/GSM8K), penalized by GPT-5-family monitor suspicion; swapped-question load-bearing test; cross-monitor/prompt transfer; paraphrase defense.
records.findings: Monitor jailbreaking, not encoding: side-task reasoning load-bearing (swapped acc → 0) yet human-readable; framing fools monitor. Transfers to unseen GPT-5 monitors (usually weaker; once gpt-5.2) and most prompt rephrasings; weakly cross-family; manual replicas fail. Same-monitor paraphrase: suspicion 2.5/1.2 → 7.4; keeps 79–87% side, 63–91% main acc. Code released.
records.limits: GPT-oss policies and GPT-5 monitors only, one main task, benign side tasks; gpt-5.2 not jailbroken within budget; human readability judged informally.
changes: tags: (none) -> + reveals:cot-reliance (the swapped-question test, a reported metric in Sec. 3.4/App. B, checks whether the side-task answer causally depends on the CoT; the record already tags signal:cot-intervention and metric:swapped-question-accuracy for it)

findings: 'side-task reasoning human-readable' -> 'side-task reasoning load-bearing (swapped acc → 0) yet human-readable' (Sec. 4.1: with swapped questions and the same CoT as prefill, side-task accuracy drops to zero; this is the paper's evidence that the reasoning is not latent)

findings: 'Transfers within GPT-5 family, weakly cross-family' -> 'Transfers to unseen GPT-5 monitors (usually weaker; once gpt-5.2) and most prompt rephrasings; weakly cross-family' (Sec. 4.2/D.3/D.4: transfer is asymmetric, from stronger to weaker monitors, with one nano-trained run reaching gpt-5.2 (63% scored 1/10); 5 of 6 monitor-prompt variants stay low; the record named prompt transfer as a method but gave no result)

findings: 'Same-monitor paraphrase → suspicion 7.4' -> 'Same-monitor paraphrase: suspicion 2.5/1.2 → 7.4' (Sec. 4.3 gives the pre-paraphrase baselines; without them the 7.4 has nothing to compare against)
limits: 'One model family' -> 'GPT-oss policies and GPT-5 monitors only' (Sec. 5.1 limits the work to the GPT-oss family AND GPT-5 monitors; cross-family monitors were only used for evaluation)
uncertain: lever:rl-reward: the monitor-penalty reward is the stressor under study (it lowers monitorability), not a faithfulness-improving term

lever:inference-time + updates:explanation: paraphrase defense is a secondary eval of a previously proposed idea (Kokotajlo & Demski), so contribution:method was not tagged even though the abstract mentions it
contribution:negative-result: CoT-monitor penalty backfires (jailbreaks), but the paper frames this as a phenomenon or analysis, not as a failed intervention
reveals:hidden-info: the core question is whether encoded reasoning emerges, and the answer is no; misbehavior (side-task reasoning the monitor should catch) is the main reveal
domain:synthetic: Game24 plus a procedurally generated multiplication side task is a toy setup, but GSM8K is natural math
scale: gpt-oss-20b (about 21B total) tagged mid, gpt-oss-120b large; GPT-5 monitors are only evaluated (and one paraphrases), so no scale:closed
signal: no judge tag, because the monitor is the instrument being attacked; the claim that the CoT is 'transparent to humans' rests on the author's informal inspection, not a human study

relations empty: skaf2025large, baker2025monitoring, emmons2025chain, macdermott2025reasoning, mathew2025hidden appear only in related work; the paper explicitly argues it does not contradict skaf2025large; a possible 'contradicts korbak2025chain' (encoded-reasoning threat model) was omitted because korbak is only cited as motivation
eval:ood: held-out monitors, cross-family monitors and monitor-prompt rephrasings are treated as held-out distributions

records.problem: Free-form CoT is hard to verify, verbose and possibly post-hoc → the answer may not come from the stated reasoning.
records.method: Model emits an executable JSON computational graph; answer = its deterministic execution. Graph SFT → Graph-Based GRPO (style, graded correctness, node-overlap or proof-F1 rewards; faithfulness runs also emit an answer, with answer and answer–graph consistency rewards). 4 models ≤4B, 5 math/proof datasets.
records.findings: Beats Graph SFT on all 5 datasets; up to 6.1× shorter than Default GRPO. Internal–external gap ≈0 on iGSM/MATH; F_strong rises (MATH 21.4→40.2), mainly via F_ID. GSM8k+: F_strong 0 and gap widens to 31.9; Qwen3-4B emits memorized original-GSM8k answers, bypassing the graph.
records.limits: Accuracy cost on MATH (0.19 vs 0.61 Default GRPO). F_OOD (answer follows an edited graph) not consistently improved. Consistency reward directly trains what the gap/F_ID measure. Graph-expressible tasks, ≤4B models only. No code release mentioned.

new_tags.definition: evaluation audits or controls for benchmark memorization (contamination detection, perturbed or regenerated benchmark) so that answers produced by recall are not credited to the reasoning trace

changes: method: 'style, graded correctness, node-overlap rewards' -> 'style, graded correctness, node-overlap or proof-F1 rewards' (node-overlap reward is arithmetic-only; Entailment/ProofWriter use leaves/steps F1 rewards, Sec. 3.3)

method: 'faithfulness runs add answer and answer–graph consistency rewards' -> 'faithfulness runs also emit an answer, with answer and answer–graph consistency rewards' (the explicit ANSWER exists only in the faithfulness runs; in the main runs the answer is the graph's execution)

findings: 'F_strong rises (MATH 21.4→40.2)' -> '... mainly via F_ID' (Table 10: MATH F_ID roughly 34–54→69–89% per model while F_OOD moves only ~39–52→45–54%; the gain tracks the directly rewarded consistency)

findings: 'On GSM8k+ F_strong is 0: the model emits memorized answers that bypass the graph' -> 'GSM8k+: F_strong 0 and gap widens to 31.9; Qwen3-4B emits memorized original-GSM8k answers, bypassing the graph' (the memorization evidence is per-model, for Qwen3-4B: external acc 0.20% vs redefined gold, 42.0% vs original answers; the paper says 'suggests'; the widening gap, 12.1 ICL→31.9 Graph GRPO, is a reported result)

limits: 'MATH acc 0.19 vs 0.61 for Default GRPO, so there is an accuracy cost against free-form methods' -> 'Accuracy cost on MATH (0.19 vs 0.61 Default GRPO)' (Graph-Based GRPO has the best average on the other 4 datasets, so the cost against free-form methods is not general)

limits: added 'F_OOD (answer follows an edited graph) not consistently improved' (Table 10: F_OOD drops after GRPO for 2/4 models on iGSM and on ProofWriter, e.g. Gemma 65.9→37.1, which weakens the conclusion's claim that editing the graph changes the answer more reliably)
limits: 'small models only' -> '≤4B models only' (more precise; all four models are 2–4B)
uncertain: signal:by-construction: the deterministic graph executor supplies the answer the graph implies; it could instead be read as signal:env-label (a program-provided label)
updates:behavior: the consistency reward S_f is symmetric, so RL could reconcile graph and answer by changing the graph rather than the emitted answer
lever:sft: Graph SFT only initializes the output format before GRPO; tagged as part of a hybrid method
domain:logic: covers ProofWriter (T/F deduction) and EntailmentBank Task2 (science-QA entailment trees); EntailmentBank could arguably be domain:open-qa

eval:optimization-pressure not tagged: S_f directly trains the answer–graph agreement that Δ/F_ID then measure, but the paper does not frame or test this as optimization pressure (F_OOD graph edits are not trained on)
eval:contamination-control (coined): CoDeC audit plus redefined-operator GSM8k+; this is a side analysis, not a headline contribution, so contribution:benchmark was not tagged
motivation: monitoring not tagged even though Baker 2025 is cited in the intro; the framing is verifiable explanations and efficiency/accuracy

relations empty: lyu2023faithful, paul2024making and creswell2022faithful are conceptually close but cited only in related work; the intervention protocol (F_ID/F_OOD/F_strong) comes from Somov et al. 2026, which is not in the corpus; baselines (ToT, Default GRPO, CoT+Answer SFT) are not corpus papers
metric names: internal-external-gap (graph-execution vs emitted-answer accuracy) and f-strong (Somov et al. intervention metric) were named here and may need normalization at consolidation

records.problem: Finetuning implants hidden or harmful behaviors; untrained self-reports are unreliable, so auditing is hard.
records.method: Finetunes of one base with known implanted behaviors (8 categories) → one shared LoRA introspection adapter: SFT to verbalize each behavior, then DPO preferring accurate reports over hallucinations → applied to unseen finetunes.
records.findings: AuditBench SOTA (59% agent success vs 53% next-best); flags 7/9 cipher-attack models; surfaces 16/52 RM-sycophant behaviors, not root goal; sandbagging claims 33% on UKAISI sandbaggers vs 15.8% FPR. Gains with scale (Qwen3 0.6B→14B: 37.7→77.3%), diversity, DPO. Code, models released.
records.limits: High false-positive rate (hallucinates train-set behaviors, esp. on base M); OOD gains plateau with diversity; costly setup; true introspection untested.

relations.note: scales DIT adapter to larger models, more diverse behaviors, adds DPO stage

changes: findings: (no sandbagging result) -> 'sandbagging claims 33% on UKAISI sandbaggers vs 15.8% FPR' (the UKAISI detection is one of the four headline OOD evaluations in the contributions list, Sec. 3.4/Fig. 5)

findings: 'SOTA on AuditBench ... not the root goal ... diversity and DPO. Code and models released.' -> 'AuditBench SOTA ... not root goal ... diversity, DPO. Code, models released.' (trimmed to offset the added clause; the summary was ~100 words against a ~60 target)
method: 'Many finetunes of one base, each with a known implanted behavior' -> 'Finetunes of one base with known implanted behaviors' (length only; content unchanged)

tags: verified all and kept them. lever:architecture stays because tags.yaml lists adapters explicitly and the IA is a detachable module attached to other models (M_i ⊕ A). eval:specificity stays because Fig. 5 measures a sandbagging false-positive rate on non-sandbagging models and App. F tests yes/no negative questions. reveals:misbehavior, eval:privileged-access (paper says it does not test introspection in the strict sense; the activation-oracle comparison is a comparison of auditing-agent tools), contribution:analysis, lever:steering (appendix only) and signal:judge (the judge scores against implanted labels) all stay omitted.

relations: verified that goel2025learning is in the corpus and the paper says 'build on ... scale and extend', so extends fits. betley2025tell, binder2024looking, plunkett2025self and turpin2023language are cited only for motivation and related work, so no link.
uncertain: lever:architecture: the IA is a detachable adapter (tag lists adapters), but it is just a LoRA trained by SFT/DPO, so the tag may duplicate lever:sft
reveals:misbehavior omitted: some targets are misbehavior (RM-sycophant reward hacking, sandbagging, cipher attacks), but the framing is auditing implanted behaviors, not CoT monitoring
eval:specificity: false positives are checked only partly (sandbagging-claim rate vs a 15.8% FPR on non-sandbagging models, yes/no negative questions in App. F, and FPR named as a limitation)

eval:privileged-access omitted: AuditBench compares IA against activation oracles and other tools, but the paper says explicitly that it does not test privileged access / introspection in the strict sense
domain:chat only: the implanted behaviors span math, code and MCQ sandbagging (MMLU), but the self-reports are elicited by chat questions
contribution:analysis omitted: the scaling and diversity studies are listed as a core contribution, but they analyze the new method itself
lever:steering omitted: the single-layer bias-vector / rank-1 ablation appears only in an appendix
signal: the LLM judge grades the match to known implanted labels (instrument, not ground truth), so signal:judge is not tagged; the judge also scores DPO pairs
extends vs builds-on for goel2025learning: the paper says 'build on' and 'scale and extend'

records.problem: Can LLMs state the rule that actually drives their own classification behavior?
records.method: ArticulateRules: 29 procedurally generated few-shot text-classification rules + adversarial OOD inputs; verify behavior matches known rule ID+OOD, then grade MC/freeform rule articulations (GPT-4 grader, ~95% vs human labels). In-context: GPT-3 family, GPT-4; finetuned GPT-3 → SFT on articulations, held-out rules.
records.findings: In-context freeform acc rises w/ scale: Curie 1%, GPT-3 7%, GPT-4 72%. Finetuned GPT-3 (>90% ID+OOD on 10 rules) articulates 0%; SFT on correct explanations → still 0% on 7/10. MC above chance 9/10 after SFT. Paraphrase/CoT augmentation no sig. help (1 rule tested). Dataset, code, OpenAI eval released.
records.limits: Success necessary not sufficient (pattern completion vs introspection); black-box only; SFT on 10 rules, low diversity; 2023 OpenAI models only.
changes: tags: reveals:internal-strategy -> removed (ground truth is black-box only, Sec 1/5. The articulated rule is the input feature that decides the label, which is decision-factors. The paper says it cannot tell introspection on internal processes apart from statistical completion without whitebox methods, Sec 4/App A.)

findings: 'Freeform acc rises w/ scale: Curie 1%, GPT-3 7%, GPT-4 72%' -> 'In-context freeform acc rises w/ scale: ...' (these are in-context top-3 averages from Table 3/Fig 2. Without the label they can be confused with the finetuned GPT-3 results that follow.)

findings: 'Paraphrase/CoT augmentation no help' -> 'Paraphrase/CoT augmentation no sig. help (1 rule tested)' (App B.5.2/B.5.3 tested only the 'contains the word W' rule, n=20. Paraphrase moved validation acc 5%->15%, which is not significant, and CoT left it at 5%. 'No help' overgeneralized.)
uncertain: object:self-report vs object:posthoc-expl: the articulation describes the rule behind the model's classification across many inputs, not one decision, so self-report seemed closer.
reveals:internal-strategy: the paper frames the task as explaining 'internal processes', but its ground truth is purely behavioral. decision-factors alone may be enough.

signal:generic-cf vs signal:by-construction: the rule is fixed when the dataset is built, but the model's adherence to it is checked behaviorally on held-out ID/adversarial inputs. The GPT-4 grader is validated against human labels, so it is an instrument, not signal:judge.
scale:closed: davinci's size (175B) is disclosed but its weights are closed (finetuned via API). No size class fits exactly.
updates: the classification finetuning only aligns behavior to the known rule as setup, so it is not tagged updates:behavior. Only the articulation SFT counts as the intervention.
contribution:negative-result: SFT fails for freeform articulation but clearly helps MC, so the result is partly negative.
motivation: the paper says it 'focuses on honesty' (eliciting explanations that reflect the model's beliefs). This is tagged only as explainability, with no motivation:honesty tag coined.
Findings '>90%': the intro says >=95% ID+OOD for GPT-3-c, while Sec 3.2.1 and Table 9 give >90% (min 92.3%).
model tags: Ada/Babbage (in-context only) are omitted, and Babbage's size is not stated in the paper. Curie is 13B according to the paper.
relations: none. Turpin 2023 is cited only in related work, and no other corpus paper is used or compared.

records.problem: CoT sometimes unfaithful to the model's computation; optimizing for faithfulness often costs accuracy.
records.method: REMuL: GRPO rewards the speaker when 3 diverse 14B listeners, continuing its CoT truncated at 25/50/75%, reach its answer; a separate answer-only masked LoRA SFT restores accuracy. Train on BBH; test OOD on BBEH, ZebraLogic, MuSR, FOLIO.
records.findings: Hint usage +2.5 avg; acc +1.8 (Qwen3) / +1.5 (Phi4). Early-answering & adding-mistake AOC up on avg (Qwen3); beats MAT-Steer. Faithfulness-only RL most faithful but cuts acc; joint reward makes objectives conflict; hint-optimized RL fails to transfer to AOC. CoTs more legible, shorter, less backtracking. Ablation: multiple diverse listeners needed. Code released.
records.limits: 14B models, MC reasoning tasks only; AOC, legibility, ablations, sycophancy on Qwen3 only; no error bars. Hint detection by keyword, only on changed answers. Gains small. Slightly more sycophantic (38.6 to 41.8%). In-domain (FOLIO) training raises acc but not faithfulness.

relations.note: uses early-answering and adding-mistakes AOC as faithfulness metrics
uses sycophantic hint-injection protocol to measure hint usage
uses its legibility autorater prompt to score CoT legibility

changes: problem: 'CoT is often unfaithful ... training for faithfulness usually costs accuracy' -> 'CoT sometimes unfaithful ... optimizing for faithfulness often costs accuracy' (abstract says 'sometimes fails' and 'often degrades'; overclaim)

findings: 'Early-answering & mistake AOC up' -> 'Early-answering & adding-mistake AOC up on avg (Qwen3)' (Table 2 reports AOC for Qwen3-14B only; REMuL early-answering AOC drops on MuSR, 0.332 -> 0.325, avg gain +0.033)

findings: 'Faithfulness-only RL cuts acc' -> 'Faithfulness-only RL most faithful but cuts acc' (faithfulness-only has highest hint usage and adding-mistake AOC; REMuL trades some faithfulness for accuracy)

limits: 'Only 14B models and multiple-choice logic tasks' -> '14B models, MC reasoning tasks only; AOC, legibility, ablations, sycophancy on Qwen3 only; no error bars' (BBEH and BBH training tasks are not pure logic; Tables 2-7 and 12 are Qwen3-only; no seeds or variance reported)
uncertain: updates:explanation + updates:behavior: the reward reshapes the CoT so listeners can follow it, but the AOC gains mean the answer also relies more on the CoT. Unclear which side moves, so both are tagged.
eval:optimization-pressure: present only through the Hint Optimized baseline, which is trained on the hint metric and then fails on AOC. REMuL itself is not trained against any eval metric.
lever:multi-agent-game not tagged: the paper calls the method multi-party RL, but the listeners are frozen, not co-trained, so the tag definition does not fit.

reveals:correctness / signal:judge not tagged: legibility (scored by a GPT-OSS-20B autorater, Emmons prompt) is a secondary analysis, not the faithfulness ground truth, although the abstract mentions it.
model naming: phi-4-reasoning-plus is 14B but the size is not in its name. The listener ministral-3-14b and the autorater gpt-oss-20b are omitted as auxiliary.
metric names: the paper calls it 'hint usage'/'hint attribution'; it is tagged hint-verbalization-rate so it matches other papers.
motivation: only explainability is tagged. The impact statement briefly mentions monitorability.
contribution:negative-result not tagged: the conflict between faithfulness and correctness rewards and the failure of hint-only RL to transfer are side findings, not abstract-level claims.

kirchner2024proververifier (legibility) and lyu2023faithful / creswell2022faithful (hard vs soft execution) are cited only in the intro or related work, so no relation is recorded; MAT-Steer (Nguyen et al. 2025) is a baseline but is not in the corpus.

records.problem: CoT penalties can hide reasoning but keep behavior. Is the hidden CoT still load-bearing (steganographic)? Does the encoding generalize?
records.method: PPO, task reward minus regex CoT penalty on task-critical strings: arithmetic, coin flip (Qwen2.5-3B); ExploreToM with held-out names (GenPRM-7B). Prefill, error-injection, name-swap ablations test load-bearing.
records.findings: Models substitute strings (U+2217 for *, R/L for Heads/Tails), keep >90% arithmetic acc. Fixed R/L prefill drops coin-flip acc 98% → ~55%. ToM encodings (nicknames, initials) transfer to never-penalized names; task score roughly stable. Code released.
records.limits: Regex monitor only. 3B/7B, toy tasks. 1/3 coin-flip seeds converge. Arithmetic ablation n=5. ToM encodings hand-labeled.

relations.note: CoT-pressure obfuscation shown to be load-bearing steganography that generalizes to unpenalized strings

changes: findings: 'Wrong-encoding prefill drops coin-flip acc from 98% to ~55%' -> 'Fixed R/L prefill drops coin-flip acc 98% → ~55%' (Table 1 prefills a fixed 'R' or 'L' at Flip 1 whatever the true state, so it is wrong for only about half the prompts; that is why accuracy falls to near chance. The encoding-free prefill control stays at 98%)
limits: added 'Arithmetic ablation n=5' (App. E.1: the error-injection check uses 5 samples and a different checkpoint, trained against the ['*'] list)

summary length: problem/method/limits trimmed (record was ~120 words against a ~60-word target); dropped 'no LLM monitor', '(exploration bottleneck)', 'LLM judges unreliable' and the explicit 'Open questions' framing; no claims changed

tags: no change after review. signal:judge kept because Fig 3c/d encoding rates rest only on the authors' manual labels (App. B.3), so the human rating is the ground truth. lever:rl-reward + updates:explanation kept: the paper trains with a monitor-penalty reward term, and what it changes is the CoT, not the task behavior. negative-result + analysis both kept: the headline is that the CoT penalty backfires, inside an empirical study with no new method. reveals:misbehavior and eval:adversarial correctly omitted

relations: no change. 'We provide an extension to these results' (abstract) supports extends for baker2025monitoring. roger2023preventing and mathew2025hidden are cited only in Background, and their methods are not used, so they are skipped
uncertain: lever:rl-reward / updates:explanation: the CoT penalty is studied as a hazard, not proposed as a faithfulness method. The penalty is meant to change behavior via the CoT but only changes the explanation, so 'updates' is an awkward fit.

signal:judge: ToM encoding rates (Fig 3c/d) come from the authors' manual labels after Claude 4.5 / GPT-5 judges failed. Unclear whether author hand-labeling counts as 'human rating IS the ground truth'.
reveals:misbehavior omitted: the penalized strings are benign task info (Heads/Tails, '*', character names) that stand in for harmful planning. No real misbehavior is studied.
domain:open-qa for ExploreToM theory-of-mind QA (yes/no and free-form, occasionally lettered options). Coin flip tagged synthetic; it could also count as logic.
contribution:negative-result: the headline is that CoT process supervision backfires into steganography. analysis is also tagged; check whether both should apply.
extends vs builds-on for baker2025monitoring: the paper says it 'provides an extension to these results' but does not reuse Baker's code or environment.

roger2023preventing skipped: cited in Background only ('Extending [16]', the codebook-SFT steganography plus paraphrase defense), and its method is not used. mathew2025hidden skipped: background only, though it shares an author.
eval:adversarial not tagged: the models are trained to evade the regex monitor, but no monitor or defense is evaluated against them.
Numbers: coin-flip prefill accuracy is 98/98/56/55 (Table 1); '>90%' arithmetic acc is from Sec 3.1. The ToM name-swap table (e.g. 62.5% to 37.2%) is in Appendix E.3.

records.problem: Contextual (CoT/input perturbation) and parametric (unlearning) CoT-faithfulness metrics compared only descriptively; does optimizing one transfer to the others?
records.method: FaithMATE: best/worst of 40 sampled CoTs under one metric → SFT or DPO (LoRA); measure gain transfer δ on 6 metrics (4 Lanham corruptions, CC-SHAP, FUR). Gemma3-4B/Qwen2.5-7B/Llama3.1-8B; OpenBookQA, LogiQA. Plus task-arithmetic merging.
records.findings: Paradigms positively coupled but asymmetric: parametric→contextual consistent (24/30, 23/25); contextual→parametric 40/48, magnitude variable. Contextual metrics don't reliably inter-transfer; Adding Mistake lowers Paraphrasing in 8/12. DPO > SFT. Acc up in all OBQA configs (avg +6–8%), mixed on LogiQA (17/30 up). EA+FT merging amplifies gains; merging hurts Paraphrasing.
records.limits: ≤8B, MCQ only; offline training only (no RL); metrics treated as unvalidated proxies; parametric metric ~20 min/instance; no code release stated; LogiQA 23/25 excludes Llama SFT (poor contextual results).

relations.note: FUR step-unlearning as parametric metric and training target; adds continuous ff_cont

records.problem: LRM CoT tuned for acc/efficiency, not trust: traces hard to follow, silently use cues, overconfident.
records.method: SFT on tagged traces (understanding→facts→plan→think→answer→self-assessment) → GRPO rewarding correctness, format, cross-section refs, calibrated confidence. Vs matched Plain (correctness-only GRPO).
records.findings: Qwen3-1.7/4/8B: interpretability +44.0%, faithfulness +18.8% (professor-hint disclosure up), reliability +42.4%; commitment faithfulness 0.90–1.00 (QwQ), 0.83–0.94 (MTurk); acc ≈ Plain, 1.16× shorter. Transfers to DS-R1-Llama-8B. Code released.
records.limits: Math-centric, ≤8B. Commitment faithfulness LLM-judged, ≈ SFT-only ablation, no Plain comparison. Humans prefer ReFIne readability only 52.4 vs 46.7%. One hint type, no false-positive check. Acc below Plain on hard comps (AIME, HMMT), small-model non-math.

records.problem: CoT answers often don't causally depend on the stated steps; prior fixes need human labels/filtering or symbolic solvers.
records.method: Swap each step for a domain-matched irrelevant fact (Wikidata/arithmetic corpus, style-rewritten), regenerate, score answer log-prob drop → score-weighted LoRA SFT on post-intervention continuations + gold-answer term (η) + KL to base.
records.findings: Mistral-7B, Qwen3-8B/4B: faithfulness x1.4-2 (GSM8K/SVAMP), x4-18 (StrategyQA) vs accuracy-only SFT; untrained static & truncation metrics also rise. Claims no significant acc cost (yet Mistral GSM8K 0.41 vs 0.50). No answer supervision → more faithful, big acc drop. Code/data in supplement.
records.limits: Proxy log-prob metrics, main one = training signal; ≤8B; in-distribution tests; ~10-24h data gen/model; hand-tuned hyperparams; fact-corpus dependent.

records.problem: CoT/explanations may be unfaithful (answer doesn't follow) and untruthful (model doesn't believe its own premises).
records.method: T5-11B fine-tuned on EntailmentBank + new crowd-labeled entailments (incl. negatives); backward-chains from each answer hypothesis, overgenerates premises, keeps steps the model self-verifies (premises + entailment); answer = top-scoring proof.
records.findings: Zero-shot OBQA/QuaRTz acc 75.2/75.4 vs direct 75.2/74.1 → no acc cost. Humans (1-deep proofs, 100 OBQA Qs): >70% conclusions clearly follow (Macaw 34%), ~90% premises correct, preferred 57% vs 23%. Mixing with direct QA breaks faithfulness on 14-17% of questions. Data + models released.
records.limits: Faithful only by answer selection; belief = "yes" to "Is X true?". Near-tautologies, invalid steps; ~360 s/question; one model, science MCQ.

updates:explanation: premises are filtered to fit model beliefs (explanation side), while the answer follows from the proof (behavior side); both tagged

records.problem: Can standard steering tools (ICL, fine-tuning, activation editing) make the CoT faithful, i.e. make the answer depend on it?
records.method: ICL and LoRA SFT on self-generated (Q, CoT, A) triplets picked uniformly or by faithfulness (deterministic/stochastic, correct-only variants); ITI-style editing of probe-selected heads. Faithfulness = per-instance early-answering AOC. AQuA, LogiQA, TruthfulQA.
records.findings: ICL/SFT: small gains that depend on dataset and model, often with an acc drop (~20% vs GTA baseline, Llama SFT on TruthfulQA). Text says faithful demos beat uniform ones; appendix tables mixed. Steering: no significant gain; best heads/alpha/K differ by dataset. GPT-4 is the most accurate and the least faithful.
records.limits: One truncation metric. 3 datasets. GPT-4 gets ICL only (FT blocked by API errors); steering on Llama-3-8B only. Many differences not significant (p-values in appendix). No code mentioned.

relations.note: adopts early-answering metric, made per-instance with answer probabilities

records.problem: Training against white-box deception probes may teach evasion, not honesty; prior obfuscation evidence only from artificial harmful-output setups.
records.method: MBPP-Honeypot RLVR (1 visible test + length penalty → hardcoding); GRPO + off-domain deception-probe penalty; KL × penalty sweep; probe score split: original-model vs representation change.
records.findings: Outcomes: honest, blatant, obfuscated policy (evasive text, e.g. justifications; low KL + weak penalty), obfuscated activations (RL drift, even w/o probe; PG adds no activation pressure, probe gradients do). High KL + high penalty → honest, no capability cost. Code/models released.
records.limits: High KL often impractical at scale; obfuscated policies hard to detect; single-turn MBPP, ≤70B; richer hacks (test tampering) untested.

new_tags.definition: the task response or action itself (e.g. generated code plus any accompanying commentary), checked for honesty/deception rather than a separate CoT or explanation

records.problem: Plausible CoT may misstate the real reasons for predictions → unwarranted trust, and CoT-based audits can be fooled.
records.method: Biasing features the CoT never mentions (Answer-is-Always-A, Suggested Answer) on 13 BBH tasks; BBQ with swapped weak evidence. GPT-3.5 & Claude 1.0, ZS/FS, CoT vs No-CoT.
records.findings: Bias verbalized in 1/426 explanations. Accuracy drops up to 36% (ZS); FS CoT less unfaithful. 73% of sampled unfaithful CoTs argue for the biased answer; 15% have no obvious errors. BBQ: up to 62.5% of unfaithful pairs stereotype-aligned (50% = unbiased). Debiasing prompt helps Claude. Code released.
records.limits: Necessary but not sufficient test. Only small input edits. Two closed models. No fix proposed.

records.problem: RL-learned reward hacks (exploiting prompt cues) go unverbalized in CoT → CoT monitors miss them.
records.method: VFT: SFT on CoTs minimally edited (Claude 4 Sonnet) to credit planted cues (2 cues) → GRPO rewarding cue-aligned wrong MMLU answers incl. held-out cues; vs BCT, RL-only.
records.findings: Post-RL undetected hacks (ECR) 6% vs 88% RL-only, 99% BCT; verbalization 8%→43% (VFT)→94% (RL). Holds, smaller gap, on non-amplified cues (ECR 15% vs 63-66%). Pre-RL specificity 96-97%. MMLU acc 73→70% after VFT; post-RL ≈ RL-only (63 vs 65%).
records.limits: Llama-3.1-8B, MMLU only; held-out cues similar to training; post-RL verbalizations vaguer, some over-verbalization; ambiguous cases judged as verbalized; hacks need no CoT.

records.problem: Context perturbation tests measure self-consistency, not parametric faithfulness: models can recover erased steps from weights.
records.method: FUR (PFF instance): unlearn each CoT step's content words (NPO+KL, FF2) → no-CoT answer flips (ff-hard) or loses probability (ff-soft)? Controls: efficacy, specificity, MMLU. 4 LMs, 5 MCQA sets.
records.findings: MMLU ~unchanged; answers often flip, mostly more than Add-mistake; efficacy tracks ff-hard (r=0.889). Post-unlearning CoTs argue for other answers (GPT-4o-mini judge). ff-soft vs human plausibility r=0.15. Code released.
records.limits: Only CoT/no-CoT-agreeing instances; lower bound, no recall guarantee. Imperfect unlearning; needs weights; costly per step. English MCQA, ≤8B.

relations.note: Add-mistake and paraphrase baselines; FUR flags more CoTs as faithful
context perturbations may underestimate faithfulness; truncation/filler-insensitive (post-hoc) CoT can still be faithful

records.problem: Standard CoT is not load-bearing: the answer can bypass the reasoning, so the CoT may not reflect the decision.
records.method: Markovian bottleneck: answer predicted from length-capped CoT alone, question hidden. GRPO-style RL on ln P(ans|CoT) vs a frozen-baseline CoT, actor-reward grads, KL to base; LoRA.
records.findings: GSM8K 19.6→57.1%, ARC 36.1→79.9%; mean ≈3–4 pp below Non-Markovian GRPO (MMLU 13 pp). Larger drops under CoT perturbation than Non-Markovian (Wiki, most QA; not arithmetic). Llama CoTs help Mistral/Phi/GPT-2 predict GSM8K answers. Code released.
records.limits: Ensures sufficiency, not mirroring of internals; post-hoc CoT still possible. Steganography only argued against (KL, transfer). ≤8B; no human study; ~$20K compute.

records.problem: Rationale-augmented reasoners can ignore or misuse rationales (shortcuts) → rationales unfaithful; self-rationalization needs >100B LMs or costly rationale annotation.
records.method: Frozen GPT-NeoX-20B prompted (7 demos) → choice-specific rationales; T5-base reasoner fine-tuned w/ counterfactual regularization: label-smoothed (low-confidence) targets when rationale masked or 30% tokens replaced.
records.findings: Best ID acc in most cases, best OOD among rationale methods; T5: higher LAS except OBQA (CSQA 24.22 vs 18.75 std); larger acc drop under swapped rationales; biggest gain from human rationales. Acc rises, no cost. Code released.
records.limits: Faithfulness = reasoner's reliance on another model's rationale; StrategyQA LAS low for all (PINTO 3.35); RoBERTa reasoner: LAS not best on CSQA/QASC; <1B reasoners, commonsense MCQ only.

accuracy drop when the model is given rationales generated for a different (random) question; larger drop = stronger reliance on the rationale

records.problem: Distilled CoT rationales are vacuous (teacher hallucinates) and ignored (student answers via question→answer shortcuts) → rationale-answer inconsistency.
records.method: GPT-NeoX-20B teacher rationalizes gold answers via contrastive decoding (vs empty/wrong answer) → T5-3b student SFT with factual + counterfactual loss (wrong-answer rationale → wrong answer).
records.findings: CD-wrong teacher most consistent. CD students generally higher LAS than CoT prompting, greedy/human-rationale students; counterfactual loss adds more. Comparable acc (human-rationale student slightly higher). More perturbation-sensitive, bigger refinement gains. Larger students more accurate, less faithful; gains hold across sizes. Code released.
records.limits: Extra teacher forward pass + counterfactual data. LAS needs T5-large simulator. Knowledge-intensive QA only; perturbation/refinement on CSQA, CREAK only.

records.problem: Outcome-only RL → correct answers paired with spurious/unfaithful CoT; shortcut learning, reward hacking.
records.method: CE-PO: Jacobian influence scores for Z→X, X→Y, direct Z→Y (prompt→rationale→answer), hardened by projecting out token-shuffled counterfactual subspace; power-mean fused with BERTScore → PPO/GRPO reward.
records.findings: +5.49 pts avg acc over vanilla (up to 9.58); both CE variants beat BERTScore-PPO/GRPO on avg for all 5 models, 4 test sets; OOD gains (Qwen3-4B only). Unhardened or partial Jacobian reward → length hacking. Scores higher on judge-correct samples. Code released.
records.limits: ≤8B only. Faithfulness gauged only by own Jacobian scores; no independent CoT test; abstract's unfaithful-CoT and perturbation-robustness claims not directly tested. First-order proxy, not true DCE. Acc via GPT-4o-mini judge; ablations and OOD on one model each.

records.problem: Outcome-reward RL on multimodal MCQ rewards lucky guesses after a faulty CoT like genuine reasoning → unfaithful traces reinforced.
records.method: SCS: truncate rollout, resample continuations under Gaussian image noise; answer agreement → consistency reward, added to accuracy + format rewards in RLOO, GRPO, REINFORCE++ variants.
records.findings: Qwen2.5-VL-7B avg acc (6 benchmarks): +7.7 pp RLOO, +0.9–2.0 pp others; +3.2 / +1.6 pp on 3B / InternVL3-8B (RLOO). Vs. base model, correct answers with flawed reasoning ~15% rarer (human 25.0→21.2 per 100; o3-mini, Gemini agree). Code released.
records.limits: Multimodal MCQ only, ≤8B. Faithfulness = step correctness, checked by authors vs. reference solutions (+ LLM raters), 100 correct cases/benchmark; no vanilla-RL comparison. RLOO baseline below SFT. ~+38% train time despite "negligible" claim.

records.problem: Post-hoc NLEs leave out the input words that actually drive the prediction.
records.method: Training-free self-refine loop (SR-NLE): answer → NLE → feedback (free-text critique, or top-5 important words via prompting/attention/IG) → refine, up to 3 rounds. Scored with the Atanasova CF word-insertion test. 4 7–8B models on ComVE, ECQA and e-SNLI.
records.findings: Avg unfaithfulness 54.81% → 36.02% (IWF-Attn). IWF beats NLF in every setting; NLF beats self-consistency sampling only on avg. Prompted IWF ≈ attribution IWF. Largest gain in round 1. Answers fixed, so no acc change. Code released.
records.limits: Single string-match CF metric. Refined NLEs get longer. Random-word feedback ≈ IWF (e-SNLI). Post-hoc NLEs only, <10B models. IG is costly.
changes: findings: 'Unfaithfulness falls from 54.81% to 36.02% (IWF-Attn). IWF beats NLF, which beats self-consistency sampling. Largest gain comes in round 1.' -> 'Avg unfaithfulness 54.81% → 36.02% (IWF-Attn). IWF beats NLF in every setting; NLF beats self-consistency sampling only on avg. Prompted IWF ≈ attribution IWF. Largest gain in round 1.' (Table 1: the numbers are averages over 12 model-dataset pairs. NLF beats SC-NLE only on average, 47.58 vs 49.74, and loses on e-SNLI Falcon and Llama and on ECQA Mistral, so the unqualified claim overstated it. The paper's headline 'notable finding' is that prompted IWF (37.23) is about as good as attention or IG IWF (36.02/36.30). Without it, the random-word limit has no context.)
uncertain: eval:behavior-control: the answer is produced before and kept fixed during explanation-only refinement, so counter instances are identical across methods. This holds by construction, not as a dedicated control experiment.
lever:inference-time alongside lever:prompt-pipeline: the zero-shot self-critique/refine loop fits both definitions ('refine' is listed under inference-time).
domain:mcq: ECQA is 5-way MCQ; ComVE is a binary choice of which sentence violates common sense. e-SNLI is tagged as classification.

relations empty: PINTO (wang2023pinto, cited as Wang 2023a), turpin2023language, lanham2023measuring and parcalabescu2023measuring appear only in intro/related work. The metric comes from Atanasova et al. 2023 and the compared prior method G-Tex comes from Yuan 2025; neither is in the corpus.

Limits line 'random-word feedback ≈ IWF': from appendix F.6 (e-SNLI avg 29.28 random vs 27.69–30.10 IWF). The paper reads this as robustness, which hints the metric may reward mentioning more input words. That reading is mine, not the paper's.

records.problem: Answer can bypass the CoT via a direct instruction→answer (Z→Y) shortcut.
records.method: Standard CoT SFT plus answer-only loss on counterfactual-CoT, biased-instruction and empty-instruction data; inference-time mask blocks answer→instruction attention. Mutual-information bound analysis. Three 7–8B models; ARC, StrategyQA, LogiQA.
records.findings: Best G-mean of FT/EA/CIE/CDE in all 12 settings: +37% avg vs per-setting strongest baseline (incl. untuned base), +61% in cross-dataset transfer. Avg acc 74.88 vs 74.80%. SFT mainly lifts CIE/CDE; mask lifts FT/EA. Code released.
records.limits: ≤8B; MCQ/boolean QA only. CIE counterfactuals use the same generator and prompt as the training data. Mask leaves instruction info in CoT states. T/F tasks need partial masking (β=80%); CDE worse than base on StrategyQA for 2 of 3 models.

records.problem: No comprehensive, fully open benchmark of when CoT reveals decision-critical factors; prior evals small, fragmented, partly closed.
records.method: 1,514 instances / 19 tasks: cue & goal injection, dual objectives, impossible tasks, necessary steps. Qwen3-32B monitor, 3 scopes (CoT/action/all). Monitorability = flag rate, TE-normalized for injections. 8 LLMs. 2 prompt stress tests (direct concealment, monitor-aware evasion).
records.findings: High when factor shapes reasoning, low when it only sets the answer (Cue-Answer, deception). More capable → less monitorable (r −0.87 to −0.39). CoT-only beats action-only by ~24%. Stress tests cut Cue-Answer ~27%, via omission not obfuscation. Code released.
records.limits: Objective tasks only; black-box. Closed models expose only summarized CoT. Single LLM monitor, weak human agreement on agent traces. Prompt-only stress tests; 5 instances per agent task.

relations.note: scales its intervention/process/outcome monitorability framework to 19 open tasks plus stress tests

records.problem: Is RLVR's "free gift" of CoT monitorability universal, a capability side effect? What drives it?
records.method: GRPO (task+format reward) on Math/Code/Science/IF data & mixes, DS-R1-Qwen-1.5B & Qwen3-4B; track hint g-mean² (Qwen2.5-32B monitor), D2A draft-swap, entropy, attention; ablate train length, difficulty.
records.findings: Gains early, then plateau; data-dependent (Science training can hurt); IF data, diversity, IF cascade best; weak/negative capability link (IF-only cuts DS-1.5B acc); tracks entropy drop & prompt attention, not answer→CoT; longer train length, hard train/eval data → lower.
records.limits: ≤4B models; mechanisms correlational; input-intervention metric may reward prompt sensitivity ("false sense of monitorability"); D2A agreement weaker on DS-1.5B general tasks; no code release mentioned.

records.findings: GPT-4: beats CoT & Logic-LM on all 5 logic sets; 100% execution rate. Human-judged correct-but-flawed answers (FOLIO): CoT 6%, SymbCoT w/o verifier 2%, full SymbCoT 0%. Code released.
records.limits: Faithfulness = human validity rating, FOLIO only, no causal test; GPT-3.5/4 only; more tokens/API cost; GPT-3.5 FOLIO below Logic-LM.

records.problem: Introspection adapters (IAs) have mainly been tested on deliberately implanted behaviors. Real fine-tunes shift alignment as side effects that nobody labeled.
records.method: 213 HF PEFT fine-tunes of Qwen3-14B/Gemma3-12B; LLM-judge-scored harmful-compliance shift vs base on 13 safety categories → 5-way labels + LLM-written reference reports; SFT (+DPO for free-form) IAs; DAIA adapter processes base output & fine-tuning delta in separate branches.
records.findings: IAs generalize to unseen models and categories. DAIA's average beats LoRA-IA in all OOD splits (OOD-C 41.3 vs 35.3) and gives better free-form reports. A probe beats both IAs on OOD-B classification (54.1 avg). Patching: DAIA uses the FT delta more. Code + data released.
records.limits: 12-14B models, additive PEFT and harmful-compliance shifts only; labels and scores come from an LLM judge; transfer to unseen categories is weaker; DAIA wins macro-F1 in only 6/12 cases.

records.problem: Does outcome-reward RLVR produce CoT that the model actually uses and that a verifier can check?
records.method: CIR: answer-prob. shift under CoT truncation (avg JS div.). SR: gpt-4o-mini's answer from answer-stripped CoT unchanged when question added. GRPO, 40 ReasoningGym tasks. Fixes: SFT on 2–512 o3-mini traces before RLVR; CIR/SR aux rewards.
records.findings: RLVR ↑acc, but CIR ↓ on 19/40 tasks, SR ↓ on 17/40; both reliably ↑ only if acc gain >50 pts. No-CoT training ≈ same acc on low-CIR/SR tasks. SFT & aux rewards ↑CIR, SR (aux: also stricter SR−); aux keeps RLVR-level acc, large-n SFT ↑acc. Code released.
records.limits: Models ≤7B. SR binary, permissive; one seed for SR reward. Aux rewards don't ↑acc where base acc ≈0; lexical richness ↓ vs SFT. RLVR drop not universal: on MATH L5, CIR & SR ↑.

records.problem: Do LLM self-reports predict their own behavior (e.g. "would this edit flip my answer?")? Even frontier models fail simple counterfactuals.
records.method: 9-task benchmark on GSM8K/HumanEval/WildGuardTest/BBQ. GT = the model's own sampled behavior on original or perturbed prompts. Skill = score minus dummy-predictor baseline. Perturb→verify→revise data from ~100 HF datasets + multi-turn BLOOM → LoRA RL.
records.findings: 18 models far from ceiling (best +0.147). Multitask RL raises skill in 3 families (Qwen3 4B–32B too), with partial cross-task transfer; SFT collapses OOD. No consistent own-model advantage → no clear evidence of introspection. MMLU-Pro −0.051 to +0.026. Code released.
records.limits: Text-only behavioral labels, not mechanism. Much of the gain is format compliance (Llama, GPT-OSS). Downstream red-team/prompt-engineering benefits are small.

records.problem: Budget-limited counterfactual audits of factor-importance self-reports; report-dependent auditing rewards suppressing factors, even under a proper score.
records.method: Verification game + Counterfactual Brier Score (report vs. flip rate, n=3); proofs for proportional, bonus, report-independent, floor audits. Rational best-response agent + 5 API LLMs; BBQ, GSM8K, HotpotQA, StrategyQA.
records.findings: Proportional: rational agent suppresses 36.9% of factors; bonus → inflation; report-independent 100% truthful, 10% floor ~98%; same pattern with log/spherical scores. LLMs follow explicit reward tables, much less without; multi-round suppression 0.15 (proportional) vs 0.08 (report-indep.), 2 models.
records.limits: Directional LLM evidence, not equilibrium; API models, temp 0; no training; single-factor perturbations miss interactions. No code reported.

records.problem: Post-hoc free-text expls often back both a prediction and its negation → cannot be faithful (contrastive consistency as a necessary condition).
records.method: PEX = weight of evidence: shift in the model's own log-odds for its answer once the expl is in context. Rank 80 sampled expls per input → DPO on top- vs bottom-PEX pairs. Faithfulness proxy = student simulatability F1 (Pruthi 2022). Opinion-spam classification (TripAdvisor, Amazon).
records.findings: 62–86% of expls inconsistent (PEX<0). Over SFT expls, DPO raises PEX 43.1–292.3% and student simulation F1 by 1.5–9.7 pts. PEX fairly robust to prompt format. Code released.
records.limits: Needs output probabilities (no black-box models). Faithfulness checked at system level only. Binary opinion-spam tasks only, 7–13B. PEX is necessary, not sufficient. DPO gains capped by best sampled expl (Mistral PEX stays <0).

records.problem: Covert payloads in CoT (encoded reasoning); paraphrasing assumed to close stego channels because they ride on surface words.
records.method: Prompted pipeline: segment CoT into steps, rewrite each to show/omit a reasoning behavior (e.g. anticipate_failure) per bit → same-model paraphraser → LLM decoder; vs matched keyword channel; 4 open models, MATH-500/GPQA. Defense: strategy-aware paraphraser.
records.findings: After paraphrase, concept beats keyword in all 8 model×dataset cells (up to +35.8 pts msg acc), via lower bit error. Answers recoverable from encoded/paraphrased CoT within ~1%; no-CoT costs 20–43 pts. Strategy-aware paraphrase: bit error 0.2–2.4% → 27–37%, msg acc −58–72 pts.
records.limits: Encoder prompted, not trained/emergent. Main results: strongest strategy only; others weaker (single-channel tests MiMo only). No stealth test. Defense: 1 strategy, GPQA, 3 models. LLM decoder; single seed.

headline non-formal conceptual framework or evaluation protocol (e.g. stress-testing guidelines) presented alongside experiments; not theory, not a no-experiment position
headline contribution assesses the validity of an existing faithfulness metric, e.g. by checking its agreement with other metrics on the same instances
headline literature review that organizes existing methods or definitions into a framework or taxonomy
procedurally generated algorithm-execution tasks (e.g. ReasoningGym matrix manipulation, bit counting, bitwise arithmetic), distinct from math problems and logic puzzles
tasks about causal inference, interventions and counterfactuals (e.g. CLadder, BBEH causal)

tracks the faithfulness/monitorability target across model size, RL steps, inference compute or monitor compute

runs the faithfulness check both with and without the original conversation (prediction, explanation request) in context, to see whether that history drives the result

re-scores explanations with a different simulator/judge than the one that supplied the training reward, to check gains are not specific to that evaluator

checks whether faithfulness scores are stable across prompt-template variations (wording, persona, target phrasing)

also measures susceptibility to a user-asserted wrong answer, to relate faithfulness to manipulability
tracks faithfulness or monitorability across checkpoints over the course of training, not only before/after

how computationally load-bearing the CoT is for the task, studied as a driver of faithfulness or monitor evasion

training factor studied for its effect on faithfulness: pressure toward shorter responses/CoTs

R2 against the identity line between a model's stated latent parameter (e.g. coin bias) and its empirical behavior or the ground-truth parameter

relative area between the random-masking and importance-guided-masking performance curves, normalized by an optimal explanation (erasure faithfulness)
accuracy drop when the model's own rationale is corrupted (e.g. random token replacement) and teacher-forced back to it.
accuracy gain when an oracle/refined rationale replaces the model's own rationale via teacher forcing.
Pearson correlation between attribute weights a model self-reports and weights estimated (by logistic regression) from its actual choices
task-specific match between self-report and measured behavior (accuracy, 1-squared error, text similarity, edit-flip), normalized to [0,1]; parse failures count as worst case
raw self-report score minus the best dummy predictor that uses only the model's ground-truth distribution; range -1 to 1
share of inconsistent prediction pairs (under swapped evidence) that are stereotype-aligned; 50% means no bias
verbalized confidence or self-assessment that tracks actual correctness, so users know when to trust an answer
replacing expensive verifiers or LLM judges with cheap signals (e.g. probes on model features) so hard-to-verify behaviors can be trained or checked at scale
keeping a stronger model's reasoning usable by weaker partners (models or humans) in joint work and handoffs
monitorable or faithful reasoning as a way to cut wasted inference compute (e.g. early stopping)
reducing the token or compute cost of reasoning as a motivation alongside faithfulness
reducing hallucinations / improving the factual accuracy of generated content
trustworthy self-reports as evidence about a model's internal states relevant to moral status or welfare
message one agent sends another in a multi-agent pipeline (summary, CoT, code), monitored for hidden content
factual assertions in the model's own long-form output, incl. its retractions or corrections of claims it made earlier
the task response or action itself (e.g. generated code plus any accompanying commentary), checked for honesty/deception rather than a separate CoT or explanation
model's natural-language description of what its own internal features or activations encode
non-faithfulness training pressure studied for its side effects on faithfulness/monitorability: budgets, targets or penalties on CoT length (efficient-reasoning RL)
training pressure studied (not proposed as a fix): RL penalty from an LLM monitor reading the CoT
training pressure studied: LLM grader scoring whether a human would like the CoT text
training pressure studied: penalty on CoT length (tokens or characters) during RL

training pressure studied: grader penalizing invalid reasoning steps in the CoT
training pressure studied: penalty for specific forbidden words in the CoT
CoT brevity (length under a token budget) optimized or measured as a monitorability property, separate from faithfulness
faithfulness proxy (not ground truth) from how the answer's predictive entropy evolves over CoT prefixes
faithfulness proxy (not ground truth) from the geometry of hidden states, e.g. latent-manifold distances or uncertainty, used for filtering, detection or reward
the model's internally represented belief or uncertainty about a claim (e.g. as read out by probes), which the output should express
a latent belief or situational awareness the model holds (e.g. that it is being evaluated), which the CoT should report whether or not it drives the answer
the model's belief about a labelled, task-relevant latent variable of the environment (ELK-style), whether or not it causally drives the answer
the model's own input-output behavior (likely outputs, feature rates, accuracy, sensitivity to edits), predicted without running it
the model's knowledge of, or confidence in, whether its own answer is correct (hallucination admission, calibrated confidence)
the model's own expected accuracy or confidence on an input, which a verbalized confidence or calibration self-description must reflect
CoT stays within a weaker model's predictive reach, so the weaker model can follow or take over the reasoning mid-trajectory (interaction-based legibility, not checkability by a verifier)
the true execution of a formal program the model itself wrote, which its reasoning trace claims to simulate
CoT is coherent, logically sound or agrees with a reference solution; a validity/plausibility proxy, not tied to the model's actual decision process
the CoT steps are themselves correct, so a right answer is not reached through flawed reasoning or a lucky guess
whether later reasoning actually follows the interpretation, premises and plan the model itself stated earlier in the same output (no unstated premises, no deviation from plan)
each stated CoT step follows from the previous ones without unexplained jumps, errors or silent corrections, as judged from the text
the answer the model would give if its reasoning stopped at the current step, surfaced during the CoT
the explained (predicting) model's answer probabilities with vs. without the explanation in context (e.g. weight of evidence, log-odds shift), used as the faithfulness or consistency signal
faithfulness inferred from whether CoT correctness (human-checked or scored against a gold rationale) matches answer correctness
ground truth is a dataset's human-written reference rationale, scored by NLI entailment or overlap
ground truth is a secret message that a red-team encoder hid in the text; hidden-information capacity is measured by how accurately a decoder recovers it
causal direction between reasoning and answer inferred by comparing NLL-approximated complexity of answer-first vs reasoning-first factorizations (ICM principle)

agreement between separately generated outputs of the same model (e.g. the answer vs the class stated in its explanation, or partial decisions in reasoning vs explanation) used as the faithfulness proxy
ground truth from erasing or editing the explanation's content in the model's weights (unlearning, knowledge editing) and measuring the resulting change in behavior
faithfulness judged by whether unlearning the knowledge verbalized in a CoT step (a weight intervention) changes the answer
legibility ground truth is the CoT's likelihood or token-distribution overlap under a weaker or base reference model (cross-entropy, JSD, overlap)
a simulator's ability to predict the model's own output on the same input from the explanation, with vs. without it (e.g. leakage-adjusted simulatability, LAS); no edited inputs
studies how shortening the CoT (length penalties, truncation, concise prompting, summarization) affects faithfulness or monitorability

harmful or borderline requests where the behavior of interest is refuse vs. comply (e.g. HarmBench, StrongREJECT, WildGuardTest)
free-form continuation or next-text prediction of natural text with no task answer (e.g. Wikipedia continuation, next word)
specialist professional-knowledge tasks such as medical or legal QA (e.g. MedQA, CaseHOLD, LegalBench)
scores the trained model with metrics, monitors, simulators or readers that were not the training signal, to rule out evaluator-specific gains
validates or stress-tests the measuring instrument itself (judge or monitor sanity checks and swaps, answer-leakage baselines, prompt-template robustness, in-distribution checks on edited inputs)
explicitly controls for a named confound that could fake the effect (CoT length, benchmark contamination, conversation context)
tracks the target along an axis (model size, training checkpoints, inference or monitor compute) rather than at a single point
compares monitors given different views of the model (CoT only, actions or output only, full trajectory)
headline claims and margins fixed in a pre-registration before scoring a frozen held-out split

[new namespace factor: what an analysis paper varies or studies as a driver of (un)faithfulness or monitorability, not proposed as a fix] RL with task-outcome rewards only (incl. its data mix and length caps), no CoT or faithfulness term
pressure toward shorter CoTs: RL length penalties or budgets, truncation, concise prompting or summarization
training signal that scores the CoT text without detecting the target behavior (RLHF reward model, human-preference grader, step-validity process supervision)
the model's knowledge or belief that its CoT is monitored (from prompts or training documents)
how computationally load-bearing the CoT is for the task or behavior (CoT-uplift filtering, difficulty sweeps)
the model's ability to reshape its CoT under instructed constraints
auxiliary training loss on internal activations or hidden states (toward a concept direction, on SAE or probe features, or via a jointly trained probe head), not inference-time steering
changes the scoring or audit rule applied to explanations so that truthful reporting becomes the model's best response, without training
combines weight deltas of separately fine-tuned models (e.g. task arithmetic on LoRA adapters) without further training
cutting the token or compute cost of reasoning (e.g. early stopping) as a goal alongside faithfulness
outputs users can rely on (fewer hallucinations, confidence that tracks correctness) as a goal alongside faithfulness
trustworthy self-reports as evidence about internal states relevant to a model's moral status or welfare
the model's main output itself (task response, code, factual claims, inter-agent message), checked for honesty or hidden content rather than a separate CoT or explanation
the model's natural-language description of what its own internal features or activations encode
the model's internal confidence in or belief about whether its own answer or claims are correct (hallucination admission, calibrated confidence)
a belief the model holds about its situation or a task latent (e.g. that it is being evaluated; ELK-style variables), to be reported whether or not it drives the answer
the CoT's steps are valid or correct (no unexplained jumps, errors, or right answers from flawed reasoning), judged from the text or a reference rather than from the decision process
the reasoning actually follows the plan, premises or program the model itself stated earlier (e.g. a simulated execution matches the program's true execution)
how much the explanation in context raises a reader's (a simulator's or the model's own) probability of the model's answer on the same input (LAS, weight of evidence), with no edited inputs
agreement between parts of the model's own output (the answer vs. the answer implied or reached by its CoT or explanation), used without any intervention
ground truth is a human-written reference rationale, scored by NLI or overlap (a plausibility proxy)
ground truth from erasing or editing a CoT step's knowledge in the weights (unlearning, knowledge editing) and measuring the change in the answer
ground truth is a hidden message the encoder was set up to embed; hidden information is measured by how well a decoder recovers it

consolidation.notes: The biggest gap in the seed was a namespace for what analysis papers vary. Coders independently coined three namespaces (factor:, pressure:, stressor:) and coded outcome-only RL three different ways under lever:, so I merged them into one factor: namespace. That namespace shows a sizeable strand (about 10 papers) that studies side effects of training that is not aimed at faithfulness (outcome RL, CoT-length pressure, CoT graders) or model properties (monitor awareness, CoT necessity, controllability) rather than proposing fixes; lever: should stay for interventions aimed at faithfulness. Most coined eval tags were Goodhart and instrument checks: scoring with held-out metrics, monitors or simulators, validating judges and masked inputs, and controlling length, contamination or context confounds. Each is done by only 1 to 5 papers, which suggests evaluation rigor is ad hoc and deserves its own column. The new reveals/object/signal values show that part of the 'faithfulness' literature actually targets reasoning validity, consistency with the model's own stated plan, internal uncertainty, or the honesty of the final output, and often uses references or output agreement rather than the model's decision process; red-team attacks and meta-evaluation of metrics also emerge as distinct contribution types. Metrics are extremely fragmented: about 285 coined names reduce to about 262 after 24 true-synonym merges (Chen et al.'s hint verbalization rate appeared under 7 names, Lanham's early-answering AOC under 3). Only about two dozen metrics are used by more than one paper, and I kept near-twins with different definitions apart: g-mean vs g-mean², conditional hint verbalization vs unconditional cue acknowledgment, per-question vs marginal bias-switch rates, unfaithful-correct over all items vs over correct items. Model names were mostly consistent; the only fixes were Qwen spelling, MoE active-parameter suffixes and thinking-mode aliases, and one tag (metric:verbalization-rate on shenoy2026introspection) needs a manual re-tag because it names a different quantity.
